"A configuration definition moves through active, deprecated, and internal states, and the runtime resolves an effective value per tenant from either the platform default or a tenant override. Setting an override performs an audit-first upsert and clearing it performs an audit-first delete, after which a best-effort change-notification event is emitted; the audit precedes the persistence mutation so the change is always recorded."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"A custom domain progresses through an explicit lifecycle: creating an ownership challenge yields a pending-DNS state, verifying the expected DNS TXT token moves it to verified, activating the auth client moves it to active, and proving local routing moves it to a routing-locally-active state. From there a domain can be set or unset as canonical, deactivated (which clears auth-client, canonical, and routing state), or disabled (which frees the enabled-domain claim while retaining history)."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"A failing or unavailable readiness probe yields a typed degraded/readiness failure for that service and never fabricates a ready state; mutation boundaries stay closed and the aggregate reflects the worst-case truth. Tenant data loss is possible only if backup/restore/export semantics are bypassed, so recovery preserves the tenant boundary and audit lineage."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"A missing route file or OpenAPI file raises an error; strict mode exits non-zero on any drift; report-only mode exits successfully while warning with explicit drift lists. The hard gate fails closed so undocumented or mismatched routes cannot pass."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"A non-2xx receiver response moves a delivery from retry to dead after bounded attempts, an unknown subscription returns not-found with null metrics, no enabled subscriptions reports no-subscriptions, and dead deliveries report a has-dead-deliveries state. An unavailable seeded organisation is skipped honestly in proof rather than reported as success."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"A non-system-admin, an empty or whitespace reason, and an empty target organisation are all rejected before audit or session creation, and a support-mode actor lacking an effective organisation cannot access a tenant FQDN. Invalid requests create no session."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"A runtime domain-identity matrix proof validates host classification plus live slug resolution, and a custom-domain resolution proof validates live registry resolution with rejection of inactive, pending, and disabled domains and a unique-enabled-domain guard. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"A set operation emits the definition's configured change audit action and a clear operation emits a value-cleared audit action, in both cases before the tenant settings are mutated and carrying key and value metadata. Audit emission is a precondition for the write, so a failed audit prevents the persistence change entirely."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"A unit proof covers group lifecycle and validation and a UI semantic harness proves the headless journey, demonstrated in source lineage via hermetic behaviour/state validation plus a semantic harness for future UI generation. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"A unit proof covers key lifecycle and authentication, and runtime proofs validate the live repository, crypto, and row-level isolation plus live route-handler behaviour including entitlement gating, demonstrated in source lineage via hermetic/runtime validation. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"A unit proof covers the contextual audit semantics and an adjacent runtime history proof validates live read-only audit/history projection, demonstrated in source lineage via hermetic/runtime validation. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"A unit proof covers the deny-by-default state machine and runtime proofs cover the entitlement seam, permission-before-entitlement ordering, the live data substrate, and the routes, demonstrated in source lineage via hermetic and live-substrate validation. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"A unit proof covers the state machine and validation and a UI semantic harness proves the headless journey, demonstrated in source lineage via hermetic state/validation proof plus a semantic harness for future UI generation. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"A unit proof covers the workflow and session state machine and a runtime proof covers the approval flow, demonstrated in source lineage via hermetic local workflow/session state-machine validation. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"A worker emits a heartbeat to mark itself alive, claims a pending event from the event substrate, runs its registered handler, marks the event processed, idempotently skips events already processed, retries a failing handler, dead-letters the event once maxAttempts is reached, and exposes its liveness. The runner consumes the durable-queue records produced by the event bus and applies retry, dead-letter, and redrive-compatible semantics so deferred work executes exactly-effectively once. Provider failure degrades readiness and keeps mutation boundaries closed rather than processing unsafely."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"A workflow starts into running, an approval.requested signal moves it to waiting, approval.granted completes it, approval.denied fails it, and an explicit cancel moves it to cancelled, with provider status read back through the orchestrator. Approval gates therefore drive deterministic state transitions and a denied approval fails the workflow rather than silently proceeding, while scheduled-job dispatch enqueues work onto the event substrate. Provider failure (Temporal or the in-memory orchestrator) degrades readiness and never falls back unsafely."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Access decisions and policy/reconciliation changes are recorded as auditable events before edge configuration is applied, preserving tenant boundary, the decision reason, and DSR/GDPR evidence. A missing tenant-isolation or audit signal on a clickthrough decision is an explicit alert condition."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Activation and deactivation emit auth-client activated and deactivated audit events with safe, domain-only metadata before the auth-client port mutation. Audit precedes the external change, so the attempt is always recorded even if the provider call later fails."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Activation and deactivation require the tenant-scoped domain-write permission, and the domain-only operation no longer requires the broader auth-settings write permission. Operations are tenant-isolated to the owning tenant's domains."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Activation refuses not-found, not-verified, and already-active before any audit or external mutation, and deactivation refuses not-found and not-active. These guards run ahead of side effects so an invalid request never reaches the auth-client port."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Adapters validate provider readiness before use, validate and normalise SDK/HTTP responses into canonical DTOs, and require idempotency keys on payment and usage operations to make retries safe. Amount, currency, subscription status, and invoice status are validated as explicit fields rather than free text."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Admin secret routes require platform.secrets.read or platform.secrets.write and are operator-only; there is no tenant UI surface in this pass. Tenant isolation prevents one organisation from resolving, reading, or enumerating another organisation's ref, enforced at the store layer. This is a security-sensitive capability, so permission, audit, and fail-closed behaviour must be preserved on every path."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Admin workflow operations require platform.workflow.* permissions (read for inspection, write for start, signal, and cancel), while exposed tenant read surfaces use tenant.workflow.read. Workflow ids are tenant-bound and the canAccess predicate denies cross-tenant access, so an operator or tenant cannot drive or observe another tenant's workflow. Tenant context, secrets, and provider credentials do not cross the capability boundary except through the declared contract."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Aggregates application and audit logs into a queryable log store and exposes a tenant-scoped search contract (log search plus an observability readiness query) that admins use to investigate behaviour within a single tenant boundary. The capability is provider-backed and tenant-data-owning, so the lifecycle/readiness model must be preserved unchanged across extraction and every search request carries and enforces the tenant context."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Aggregates readiness across composed providers into a single readiness spine so the platform can report, honestly, whether all composed dependencies are usable; it is neither provider-backed nor database-backed and owns no tenant records. It deploys the V1-proven contract GET /api/admin/providers/readiness and must keep its lifecycle/readiness model unchanged during extraction. Rollback restores the previous contract/config implementation and re-runs proof:composed-provider-readiness before promotion continues."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Alert-rule changes, incident transitions, and notification dispatch are recorded as auditable actions before the effect is acknowledged, correlated to request and trace identifiers. The audit trail preserves the suppression vs. sent distinction and must agree with proof output when a readiness or incident claim depends on it."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Alert-rule inputs (comparator, threshold, severity) and incident transitions are validated against allowed values and the legal state machine before being applied, and missing or invalid configuration fails closed. Signal and alert names are constrained to the controlled observability vocabulary so arbitrary names are not accepted as canonical."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Alert-rule, incident, and signal operations are admin-gated under standard platform security controls, with row-level-security enforcing tenant boundaries on stored signals and incidents. Permission and fail-closed checks are preserved across extraction so an unauthorised or unscoped caller cannot read or mutate alert/incident state."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"All domain operations are tenant-scoped through domain read/write permissions, and auth-client mutation is performed via an injected auth-client-domain port only after ownership has been verified. Cross-tenant enabled-domain claims are rejected so one tenant cannot claim a domain already enabled for another, preserving tenant isolation over the global domain namespace."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"All failures are fail-closed: an unauthenticated session lookup returns an unauthenticated/401 result, callback failures redirect to the login page with a generic sign-in error, and session-store lookup failure falls through to unauthenticated without leaking provider detail. Administrative failures map to typed outcomes such as validation error, no-tenant, no-credential, invalid-credential, forbidden-realm-operation, realm-unreachable, not-found, issuer-mismatch, JWKS-invalid, unreachable, and invalid-document; provider failure returns a typed degraded/readiness result, keeps mutation boundaries closed, and never fabricates successful provider state, and inactive or unknown custom hosts degrade to the platform realm rather than being trusted."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"All four sub-capabilities are tenant-scoped under the canonical row-level-security predicate (tenant isolation plus the dedicated bypass role), so one tenant cannot see or affect another tenant's retention policies, holds, or residency. Setting or releasing a legal hold and managing retention policies are privileged operations attributed to an actor; residency placement is enforced fail-closed against the tenant's home region. The retention worker operates under a system-admin/bypass context to evaluate candidates across the tenant's protected tables."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"An assert operation throws a typed denial once a quota is exceeded or the entitlement is revoked, while evaluation returns explicit denied decisions distinguishing no-entitlement from exceeded; no-quota resolves to allowed. Failures fail closed and do not grant usage on ambiguous provider state."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"An assert operation throws once the limit is exceeded while an evaluate operation returns denied decisions distinguishing entitlement denial from exceeded state; when the cache provider is unavailable it reports degraded and falls back to relational counting. Decisions fail closed on ambiguous provider state."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"An operator creates a schedule, the enabled job persists, a due tick enqueues a platform event, a same-window tick deduplicates so no duplicate event is enqueued, pausing disables due enqueue, run-now enqueues an event immediately, and an operator patch toggles the enabled flag. Scheduled dispatch is built directly on the event substrate, so an enqueued job becomes an ordinary platform_events record (for example a report.run event) carried by the durable-queue retry and dead-letter machinery. The daemon tick is invocable even though the continuous daemon loop is not claimed wired."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"API contracts are a tenant rate-limit read, an operator per-tenant rate-limit read, and an operator per-tenant rate-limit update, with developer-portal exposure of rate-limit summaries. The interface is a rate-limit port with both a cache adapter and a relational adapter behind it."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"API key creation/revocation and rate-limit policy changes carry actor metadata and audit safe metadata before the change; secrets and hashes are never emitted into audit. Read-only portal/docs access is not a mutation audit."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"API key lifecycle is explicit: creation returns a plaintext secret exactly once, listing exposes metadata only, authentication validates a live non-revoked secret, and revocation sets a revoked timestamp after which authentication returns no actor. The plaintext secret is never persisted or re-shown."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"As a shared platform-governance asset it owns no tenant-scoped records and exposes no tenant-mutating routes, so standard platform security controls apply rather than per-tenant authorization. Authority over changes flows through the USF constitutional and authority order (semantic definitions, ADRs, validators, proof, then source), not through end-user roles. Its effect on tenants is indirect: it constrains shared platform behaviour without owning or exposing tenant data."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Audit records only safe metadata such as alias, the names of changed fields, a has-secret flag, a secret-changed flag, configuration key names, and readiness result. Audit is emitted before the secret-bearing provider or storage write, so a failed audit blocks the mutation and no raw secret value is ever audited."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Auth-client activation transitions a domain from inactive to active only after ownership is verified, the activation audit is emitted, and the auth-client port successfully adds the redirect origin; deactivation transitions active back to inactive, removes the origin, and clears canonical and routing state. The external auth-client mutation is the final, gating step so the registry only reflects activation that actually took effect."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Authentication state moves unauthenticated -> authenticating -> authenticated or denied, materialised as a session record carrying session id, user id, tenant and organisation id, roles, resolved permission bundle, display name, and expiry, with no-membership and system-admin sessions holding empty tenant context by design. Administrative state includes per-tenant identity-provider definitions (alias, enabled, masked secret, scopes, issuer/JWKS validation result), OIDC discovery validation states, MFA mode (none/optional/required with TOTP or WebAuthn), lockout thresholds, and session lifespan policy. Custom-domain callback derivation depends on a domain's verified-and-active state, falling back to the platform realm for inactive or unknown hosts."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Backup and restore are operational scripts, not an owned schema: backup dumps the canonical relational database and compresses it to an owner-only, version-control-ignored local artifact, while restore destructively overwrites a target database from such an archive. Scope is the canonical relational store only; rebuildable cache, the analytical mirror, and object storage have no platform backup script because they are not canonical state and recover via provider-native lifecycle. The capability owns no tenant records, so its backup scope is configuration and evidence and a restore cannot itself create tenant data."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Backup artifacts are written with owner-only permissions to a controlled, git-ignored location so dumps are not inadvertently exposed or committed. Operator actions are environment-gated and explicit, leaving the override or confirmation token as the human-attributable signal that a destructive operation was deliberately authorised. Promotion and readiness proof logs record that the backup proof executed."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Backup validates the environment guard (refusing non-dev/test environments absent the explicit allow override) before dumping; restore validates both the dev/test environment constraint and the exact confirmation token before overwriting. The stage-level destructive-allowed and data-preservation settings from the environment registry further gate whether destructive operations may run at all in a given stage."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Because it can affect tenant-visible data or access, it must preserve tenant isolation: visibility classifications (tenant_scoped_safe vs global_only vs not_exposed) and entitlement keys gate what each tenant can see and reach. Mutating operations are administrative and must keep mutation boundaries closed on failure. Tenant-scoped reads and clickthrough access are governed by the recorded visibility and entitlement model."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Because it is read-only there is no mutation to roll back; failures return a typed degraded or readiness error rather than a partial or fabricated result, and the read fails closed when tenant context or the substrate is unavailable. Provider failure keeps boundaries closed and does not invent history entries. Tenant data cannot be exposed across tenants."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Because it owns no tenant mutation, its audit concern is the recorded classification lineage: changes to a provider's environment posture are captured as reviewable configuration/semantic changes. Readiness and audit stay visible in degraded mode. This preserves an honest, inspectable record that prevents posture inflation."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Because it owns no tenant mutations its audit concern is the auditable governance record: changes to the foundation move through Git history, ADRs, and validator findings, which form the durable evidence trail. Readiness and audit signals remain visible even in degraded mode so the foundation's posture is always inspectable. Audit here is about preserving honest lineage of decisions, not row-level mutation logging."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Because it owns no tenant mutations, its audit concern is the recorded classification lineage: changes to whether a service is shared or environment-specific are captured as reviewable configuration/semantic changes. Readiness and audit remain visible in degraded mode. This preserves an honest record of isolation decisions."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Because it performs no tenant mutation, its audit concern is the accessibility evidence record: the per-surface landmark/role/ARIA/axe results form the reviewable proof of conformance. These results remain visible so accessibility posture is inspectable. Recovery re-runs the e2e accessibility spec so the conformance claim stays evidence-backed."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Because it performs no tenant mutation, its audit concern is the integrity of the confidence record: the per-stage results and the aggregated verdict are observable evidence that promotion decisions can be traced to. Readiness and the ladder verdict remain visible in degraded mode. Recovery re-runs the verify-ladder and aggregate-confidence tests so the verdict stays evidence-backed."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Because it performs no tenant mutation, its audit concern is the integrity of the readiness roll-up: the aggregated posture is observable and the underlying per-provider signals remain visible in degraded mode. The spine preserves an honest, inspectable view rather than emitting a row-level mutation log. Recovery re-runs the readiness proof so the aggregated claim stays evidence-backed."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Because it performs no tenant mutation, its audit concern is the validation record: the duplicate list, raw-literal findings, and strict/report-only exit state form the reviewable evidence of i18n conformance. These findings remain visible so locale governance is inspectable. Recovery re-runs the validation so the conformance claim stays evidence-backed."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by a canonical-domain runtime proof that validates live registry guards, redirect-policy transition, atomic replacement, unset, and clearing on deactivation against a real substrate. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by a compliance-report composition runtime proof and an admin route-registration proof validating deterministic assembly from foundation sources. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by API-key, API-key-route, and rate-limit runtime proofs plus OpenAPI drift and GraphQL runtime contract checks against live key/rate-limit substrate. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by billing-provider port tests and external billing-provider adapter tests, including idempotent capture, refund, and live plan synchronisation against the provider. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by catalog unit tests and a catalog route-registration runtime proof, with live HTTP-backed plan synchronisation validated separately through the external billing provider adapter. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by configuration unit proofs covering branding definitions, override source, validation, and audit-first writes, together with route-level coverage of the theme bootstrap response and its default fallback. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by domain-identity-matrix and tenant-storage isolation runtime proofs plus live row-level-security isolation checks across metering, search, observability, webhooks, events, and secret-store proofs. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by metering unit tests and runtime proofs validating live idempotency, the entitlement gate, aggregation, isolation, and route handlers. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by point-in-time restore-drill, retention, legal-hold, and data-residency proofs, including the retention tick worker proven to honour active holds. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by proof:composed-provider-readiness, demonstrating that the aggregated readiness honestly reflects the underlying composed providers. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by proof:environment-registry, proof:environment-admin-bootstrap, and proof:environment-operations, demonstrating registration, bootstrap, and operational semantics. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by proof:platform-services, proof:service-clickthrough-policy, proof:service-catalog-registry, and proof:entitlements-routes together with the cited unit tests, demonstrating catalog, visibility, entitlement, and readiness semantics. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by proof:provider-config and proof:provider-readiness-contract together with the cited auth-provider-config unit tests, demonstrating configuration, credential, lifecycle, and readiness semantics. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by quota unit tests and runtime proofs validating live entitlement-before-quota ordering, exceeded state, typed denial, revoke denial, and route handlers. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by rate-limit unit tests and runtime proofs validating live relational and cache counting plus operator route behaviour and degraded fallback. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by repository substrate tests and live isolation proofs that assert RLS denies cross-tenant reads and that the checksum and migrated-state gates hold; these caught a real naive-predicate leak before promotion. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by runtime proofs covering domain challenge and verification, local routing, canonical cutover, claim lifecycle, custom-domain resolution, and custom-domain auth origin against a live substrate with injected ports. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by static-analysis, SBOM verify/policy, code-scanning validate, security-test, and security-control-route checks asserting fail-closed gate state and route registration. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by support-ticket and announcement unit tests plus a support-approval runtime proof validating the approval waiting/completed workflow and the support-session audit lifecycle. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by tenant-lifecycle unit tests and a runtime proof asserting audit-first invocation and ordered subsystem coordination with export-before-delete. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by the cited browser-to-BFF tracing end-to-end proof, which force-flushes a single Tempo trace spanning the browser app and the platform API along the observability-correlation ladder, demonstrating client-to-server trace joining as hermetic/runtime lineage rather than a current-readiness claim. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by the cited metrics (Prometheus) and dashboards runtime proofs plus observability tests, demonstrating metric exposure, trace correlation, and readiness reporting as hermetic/runtime lineage rather than a current-readiness claim. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by the cited observability-signals, alerting, incident-foundation, and alert-notification-bridge runtime proofs plus alerting tests, demonstrating rule evaluation, incident transitions, and notification bridging as hermetic/runtime lineage rather than a current-readiness claim. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by the cited platform-services and service-catalog-registry runtime proofs (and the composed-provider readiness proof), demonstrating catalog aggregation and tenant-scoped readiness reporting as hermetic/runtime lineage rather than a current-readiness claim. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by the cited service-clickthrough-policy and clickthrough runtime proofs plus service-clickthrough tests, demonstrating per-tenant access decisions and forward-auth/reconciliation derivation as hermetic/runtime lineage rather than a current-readiness claim. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by the cited tenant-observability runtime proof plus logs use-case tests, demonstrating tenant-scoped search, readiness reporting, and fail-closed isolation as hermetic/runtime lineage rather than a current-readiness claim. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by the data-governance proof and governance unit tests covering classification constraints and data-subject-request fulfilment evidence. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by the data-portability proof and portability unit tests covering resumable, idempotent import progress and no-silent-loss semantics. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by the e2e accessibility spec, demonstrating the landmark, role, ARIA, and axe expectations as a gate over UI capabilities. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by the history proof against the history repository projection, asserting the safe summarised shape and tenant scoping. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by the local backup proof, which demonstrates the guarded dump path end to end against the canonical store. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by the notification-preferences, notification-dispatch, notification-email-transport, notification-webhook-transport, and notification-transport-routes runtime proofs, described in the corpus as level-4 live Postgres, Mailpit, and webhook route validation. The proofs are the lineage evidence, not a USF readiness claim. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by the OpenAPI drift validation tests and the architecture test target asserting strict-mode exit and drift detection. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by the search, search-isolation, and search-routes proofs, including a cross-tenant isolation assertion that a foreign-tenant query returns zero rows. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by the tenant-storage-objects proof plus object-storage adapter and storage-runtime contract tests covering prefix isolation and the scan lifecycle. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by three runtime proofs: event-bus validates live Postgres outbox persistence, row-level security, and secret-payload rejection; event-worker validates processing, retry, dead-letter, and heartbeat; event-redrive validates the live admin routes and requeue, with the corpus describing this as level-4 live substrate and route validation. The proofs are the lineage evidence, not a USF readiness claim. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by three runtime proofs: secret-store-contract validates the live Postgres store contract, encryption, row-level security, and audit; secrets-openbao validates the live OpenBao provider; and provider-secrets-readiness validates the ready versus degraded classification, described in the corpus as level-4 live provider and storage validation. The proofs are the lineage evidence, not a USF readiness claim. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by two runtime proofs: scheduled-jobs validates live Postgres schedule persistence, due and run-now enqueue, row-level security, and the no-secret schema, and scheduled-job-routes validates the route handlers and access metadata, described in the corpus as level-4 live substrate and route validation. The proofs are the lineage evidence, not a USF readiness claim. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by unit proofs over the configuration use case and contract validation (definition resolution, override source, validation rules, and audit-first writes) and by an adjacent live history projection proof that validates the audit/history record of configuration changes against a real substrate. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by unit proofs over the domain lifecycle guards and by a canonical-domain runtime proof that validates live registry behaviour with an injected auth-client port. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by unit proofs over token cryptography and audit-redaction plus runtime proofs of the secret-store contract and a provider-backed secret store against a live substrate, validating that only metadata is exposed and audited. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by validate-i18n and the i18n-runtime tests, demonstrating locale resolution and the key/raw-literal/interpolation validation gate. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is exercised by webhook unit tests and runtime proofs validating signed test delivery, fan-out/retry/dead-letter, and dead-letter metrics with redrive against live storage and HTTP delivery. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is grounded in the event-worker runtime proof, which validates live Postgres claim, process, idempotent skip, retry, dead-letter, and heartbeat (level-4 live substrate validation), captured here as informational semantic lineage from the USF coverage record and equivalence audit with no source import and an open implementation language. The proof expectation is the lineage evidence, not a current USF readiness verdict. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Behaviour is grounded in workflow-closure, workflow-engine, approval-workflow, workflow-adapters, temporal-workflow-provider, and workflow-provider-live proofs, captured here as informational semantic lineage from the USF coverage record and equivalence audit with no source import and an open implementation language. The proof expectation is the lineage evidence, not a current USF readiness verdict. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Both operations are guarded environment-gated operator actions. Backup refuses to run outside development or test environments unless an explicit allow-environment override names the target, so a shared database is never quietly dumped. Restore refuses unless the environment is development or test AND a confirmation token matching the exact environment is supplied, making the destructive overwrite intentionally hard to trigger by accident."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Branding resolves from a default theme overlaid by tenant theme overrides into an effective theme response used to bootstrap the client shell, while richer branding edits (such as application name and theme selection) flow through the configuration registry as managed override definitions. The lifecycle therefore spans an unauthenticated bootstrap read and audited, permissioned branding mutations through the configuration plane."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Canonical designation is a guarded set/unset: setting is refused when the domain is not verified, the auth client is inactive, or local routing is not proven, and a successful set flips the canonical flag and the redirect policy to redirect-slug-to-canonical. A second set atomically replaces the prior canonical domain, unset clears the flag, and deactivating the domain also clears canonical."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Canonical set and unset require the tenant-scoped domain-write permission and operate only on the owning tenant's domains. The single-canonical-per-tenant invariant is enforced within that tenant's scope."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Capture, refund, subscription transitions, and dunning steps are recorded with safe metadata so financial actions are attributable, and the immutable ledger preserves the sequence of outcomes. Raw payment secrets are not emitted into audit records."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Captures browser real-user-monitoring (RUM) telemetry and propagates distributed tracing from the browser through the backend-for-frontend, so a single user interaction appears as one correlated trace spanning client and server. The browser SDK emits to a collection endpoint that forwards to the trace/log backends; the capability is provider-backed, owns no tenant records, and must keep its lifecycle/readiness model stable across extraction."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Catalog and classification are read broadly within governance scope with operator-controlled writes, while data-subject-request handling is a privileged, audited workflow. Access is constrained so that classification and request operations preserve tenant boundary and isolation, and request fulfilment is attributable to the operator who performed it. PII handling follows least-exposure so that catalog metadata never surfaces secret fields."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Catalog and readiness reads are scoped to the caller's tenant so a tenant sees only the services and readiness it is entitled to, with standard platform security controls applied. Because the readiness view can expose tenant-visible posture, isolation must be preserved and unscoped access fails closed rather than revealing other tenants' service state."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Catalog mutations record a catalog-changed audit action carrying the acting operator identity into the use-case and adapter layers, so every product/plan/price change is attributable. Route-registration proof is explicitly not treated as an audit proof; audit is a distinct, mutation-bound record."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Classification capability that places each provider on an environment-posture axis (hermetic, local, sandbox, live) while keeping provider mode and environment as separate honest dimensions; it is provider-backed but owns no database schema. It deploys the V1-proven env-classification matrix contract and must keep its lifecycle/readiness model unchanged during extraction, with migrations limited to contract/config references that update semantic artefacts when behaviour changes. Recovery re-runs proof:provider-environment-classification before promotion continues."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Classification covers port stripping, reserved slugs, malformed hosts, unknown apex subdomains, possible-custom-domain hosts, and forwarded-host precedence. Only verified active domains and known slugs validate to a tenant."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Classification model that decides whether each service is environment-specific or shared and governs the routing and isolation that follows; it is provider-backed but owns no database schema. It deploys a classification contract (V1 contract n/a) and must keep its lifecycle/readiness model unchanged during extraction, with migrations limited to contract/config references that must update semantic artefacts when behaviour changes. Rollback restores the previous classification implementation and re-runs the named proof evidence."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Classification values are validated against the constrained set (none, PII, sensitive) and request states against open or fulfilled by database check constraints, so out-of-vocabulary values are rejected. Fulfilment requires the evidence payload to be present before a request is considered fulfilled. Missing or invalid configuration fails closed rather than defaulting."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Clickthrough decisions are the permission model: access is computed from system-admin and tenant-admin resource sets and the service classification, and the resulting forward-auth sets gate edge access per tenant. This is a security-sensitive surface where permission, audit, and fail-closed behaviour must be preserved; a service not explicitly granted is denied, and dev-only services are excluded outside the appropriate context."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Configuration and contract changes are tracked as auditable platform actions with correlation to request and trace identifiers, even though no tenant records are mutated. Audit and observability signals must agree with collected proof output when a proof claim depends on a given metric or trace."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Configuration and contract changes to the telemetry pipeline are tracked as auditable platform actions correlated to request and trace identifiers, even though no tenant records are mutated. Audit and observability signals must agree with collected proof output when a correlation or readiness claim depends on a given browser-to-BFF trace."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Contract changes are audited through version control and architecture-test output rather than runtime audit rows. The gate's pass/fail result is the durable record of contract conformance at each promotion."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Contracts are the static-analysis gate, SBOM verify, SBOM policy, and code-scanning validate commands, the rule and code-scanning configuration files, and registration of an operator security route. These are CI/static contracts plus one global-operator route, not a tenant API."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Contracts expose write-only secret fields on identity-provider create/update, credential rotation, mail-sender and webhook secret writes, and a reveal-once API-key create response, all mediated by a secret-store port with provider-backed and persistence-backed adapters. No operation in the contract supports later retrieval of a raw secret value."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Contracts include support ticket create/list/update operations, a customer-health read operation, tenant announcement create/list operations, and the support-approval request/approve workflow boundary. The approval workflow is the contract boundary that must complete before privileged support access."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Contracts include the OpenAPI document, the GraphQL schema/runtime, the developer portal read operation, tenant API-key list/create/delete operations, operator tenant API-key reads, and tenant/operator rate-limit operations. The OpenAPI document is the generated client/docs contract and is held to a drift gate."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Create bodies are validated against product, plan, and price request schemas before any persistence call, rejecting malformed input with a typed validation outcome up front. Currency, billing-period, price-type, and amount fields are explicitly typed, and references between price, plan, and product must resolve."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Create, rotate-secret, and redrive mutations audit safe metadata only; redrive is audit-first and never records the signing secret; delivery attempts are durable operational records. The signing secret is excluded from every audit and metrics surface."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Create, update, and deactivate emit sub-organisation created, updated, and deactivated audit-before-change events, and audit failure aborts the insert, update, or deactivation. Read-only listing is not audited."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Create, update, and delete emit group-created, group-updated, and group-deleted audit-before-change events after precondition checks, and audit failure aborts the provider mutation. Read-only listing is not audited."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Creation and revocation emit key-created and key-revoked audit-before-change events, and a failing audit aborts creation before the key is stored. Metadata reads are not audited as mutations."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Creation is rejected for tenants without the API-access entitlement, invalid key identifiers are rejected at the route, and garbage, wrong, hash-presented, or expired secrets never authenticate. Cross-tenant listing is prevented."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Creation validates a lowercase slug's length, characters, and no edge hyphen, validates display-name length, rejects reserved slugs, and rejects a duplicate global slug, while update requires at least a display name with a length check. Invalid input is rejected before any change."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Data-subject-request fulfilment records durable evidence, and classification and catalog changes are tenant-scoped and traceable through typed logs carrying the tenant/organisation identifier and through route/use-case/provider spans that preserve tenant context. The audit trail supports compliance and evidence-pack production, and recovery must preserve the data-subject evidence alongside the records."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Database or use-case failures surface as route errors, a missing approval remains in a waiting state and does not create support access, and absent ticket/usage rows produce zero-count health signals. The approval gate fails closed so support access is not granted without approval."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Decides, per tenant and per service, whether a user may click through to an internal/composed service and derives the forward-auth allow sets plus the reverse-proxy (Caddyfile) reconciliation that enforce that decision at the edge. The capability is provider- and database-backed and owns tenant-affecting access policy, so its lifecycle/readiness model must be preserved and reconciliation kept consistent with the policy."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Decision/governance framework that classifies each capability as build, compose, adapter, defer, or reject against cost, control, and readiness criteria; its lifecycle is the lifecycle of the decision, not of a running service. It is neither provider-backed nor database-backed, so its operations are authoring, revising, and superseding decisions, each of which must update the semantic artefacts when behaviour changes. Rollback restores the previous decision/config implementation and re-runs the named proof evidence."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Delegation lifecycle is grant to active, with a duplicate active grant short-circuiting to an already-active result and no mutation, revoke to revoked, list of a tenant's delegations for authorised operators, and a self-only active-delegation lookup for non-admin grantees. Active means not revoked and not expired."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Delete refuses to continue after a subsystem coordination failure, so a failed realm deletion stops before DSR and data deletion. Tenant identifiers are validated at the route boundary and export must succeed before delete proceeds."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Durable import progress is keyed by tenant/organisation and the archive's content digest and tracks completed units plus an optional failed unit, persisted by a dedicated migration; it deliberately stores no payload or secret material. The transported payload is an encrypted compressed archive built on export and consumed on import; the canonical tenant data itself lives in the relational store and is read or written through repository ports. Progress is idempotent against re-runs of the same archive digest."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Each history entry carries an identifier, source, type, title, occurrence time, and a safe actor/status summary, returned with total, limit, and offset for paging; it deliberately excludes raw metadata, payloads, tokens, and secrets. The model is a projection over existing audit and event records rather than an owned canonical table, served through a history repository port. Paging fields make the read-only result set bounded and navigable."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Each indexed document carries a tenant/organisation id, document id, document type, title, a full-text search vector with an associated index, a URL, non-secret metadata, and an optional permission key, with uniqueness on tenant plus type plus document id. Readiness is reported as a full-text-search engine with status ready, degraded, or blocked. The index store is a tenant-scoped relational table under row-level security and excludes secret fields from indexed metadata."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Each object is represented by a registry record carrying an object id, tenant/organisation id, object key, content type, size in bytes, scan state (uploaded, quarantined, clean, or rejected), timestamps, and the tenant prefix, with storage usage tracked against a storage-bytes quota meter. Object bytes are held under a tenant-scoped key prefix in the object-storage provider, while the registry row is the relational source of truth for lifecycle and quota. The registry table is tenant-scoped under row-level security."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Each selected source is joined through an exact authored identity, path, and content-digest binding to its contract, facets, and source-specific canonical output plan. It remains an equivalence subject until the graph-generated contract projection passes semantic equivalence."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Email is format-validated and lowercased, system-admin is rejected as a tenant membership role, username format and status transitions are explicit, and the last tenant-admin cannot be demoted, disabled, or removed. Invalid input is rejected before any mutation."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Entitlement lifecycle is deny-by-default: an absent or not-granted key denies, an operator grant moves a key to granted, an operator revoke moves it to revoked, and both revoked and absent block access. Tenant self-reads project the catalog of keys as granted, revoked, or not-granted."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Entitlement reads are deterministic once the data substrate is migrated, and degraded mode disables store-dependent mutation while keeping read-only reads and audit visible. Live readiness verifies table existence, forced row-level security, no secret columns, tenant isolation, operator bypass, grant/revoke, and audit-before-change."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Environment registration and bootstrap are operator/admin actions; the capability owns no tenant data, so standard platform security controls apply rather than per-tenant roles. Bootstrap reads from the declared provider/config plane and resolves secrets through the secrets boundary rather than embedding them. Mutating the environment registry must keep mutation boundaries closed on failure."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Errors are deterministic and fail-closed: a provider or substrate failure returns a typed degraded/readiness failure instead of fabricating successful provider state or empty-but-authoritative results. Error logs carry the organisation id when tenant-scoped, mutation and side-effect paths stay closed under failure, and no partial result is presented as complete."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Errors are fail-closed: an unknown workflow read or invalid id is a typed error, an unavailable provider is a readiness/degraded state rather than a fabricated success, a denied approval yields failed, a cancel yields cancelled, and a cross-tenant access attempt returns false. Degraded mode disables mutation and side-effect paths that depend on the provider adapter while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Errors include forbidden, reason-required, invalid-target, wrong-tenant FQDN denial, and audit-backend failure that prevents session creation; every path is fail-closed. No session is created when validation or audit fails."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string
"Excluded as not-applicable-final (capability matrix); retained as lineage only, not an implementation extraction target."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Exposes a browser telemetry collection contract and OTLP browser-trace propagation to the trace backend behind ports/adapters, so the RUM SDK, collection receiver, and collector are swappable without changing the contract. Trace context propagation across the browser-to-BFF boundary is the load-bearing semantic, and emitted metric/span names follow the stable per-capability convention."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Exposes a tenant-scoped log search operation and an observability readiness query behind ports/adapters, so the log-store provider (e.g. a Loki-style backend) is swappable without changing the contract surface. Inputs are validated and normalised before reaching the adapter, and the response shape (matched entries plus readiness state) is stable so callers and dashboards depend on semantics, not provider internals."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Exposes a tenant-scoped platform services readiness query backed by a provider readiness-probe port, so individual service health checks are swappable without changing the catalog contract. The aggregate response has a stable shape (per-service identity plus readiness state) and composes with the composed-provider readiness spine for end-to-end readiness reporting."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Exposes an access-decision operation that returns granted/denied with a reason and a clickthrough URL, behind ports/adapters so the reverse-proxy reconciler is swappable without changing the policy contract. The derived forward-auth sets and reconciled proxy configuration are the contract's side effects, kept deterministic so the edge enforcement always matches the computed policy."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Exposes operations to read observability signals, manage alert rules, and view/transition incidents behind ports/adapters, plus a readiness query, so the metric/log providers and notification bridge are swappable without changing the contract. Alert evaluation deterministically maps samples to no-data/within/fired and fired alerts drive incident creation and notification dispatch with stable, well-defined transitions."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Exposes platform metrics and distributed traces through an admin observability metrics contract and an observability readiness query, giving operators time-series and span visibility into platform behaviour. The capability is provider-backed but owns no tenant records; it affects shared platform behaviour and must keep its lifecycle/readiness model stable across extraction."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Failures are deterministic and fail-closed: a checksum mismatch or a failing migration aborts the run, rolls back that file's transaction, and records nothing, so the operator fixes forward and re-runs safely. Missing or invalid configuration fails closed rather than inventing defaults, and provider failure returns a typed degraded or readiness error while keeping mutation boundaries closed and never fabricating successful provider state. Tenant data is never silently dropped or remapped; rollback is forward-fix or a guarded restore only after migration lineage is verified."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Failures are deterministic and fail-closed: a request cannot be marked fulfilled without evidence, invalid classifications are rejected, and provider failure returns a typed degraded or readiness error while keeping mutation boundaries closed and not fabricating provider success. Tenant data is never silently dropped or remapped, and the incident class is tenant-data-or-security because mishandling carries privacy exposure risk."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Failures fail closed: provider or dependency failure returns a typed degraded/readiness failure, mutation boundaries stay closed, and successful provider state is never fabricated. The principal risk is semantic drift or configuration loss rather than tenant data loss. Repeated typed errors past threshold, blocked readiness, or a failing promotion proof/smoke check are alertable foundation conditions."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Gate capability that asserts landmark, role, ARIA, and axe expectations as a contract over UI capabilities and gates promotion on them; it is neither provider-backed nor database-backed and owns no tenant records. It deploys the V1-proven e2e accessibility spec contract and must keep its lifecycle/readiness model unchanged during extraction, with migrations limited to contract/config references. Recovery re-runs the e2e accessibility spec before promotion continues."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Gate/governance capability that defines a stage-aware end-to-end confidence ladder gating promotion across hermetic, integration, staging, and production-shaped stages without upgrading proof posture by implication; it is neither provider-backed nor database-backed. It deploys the V1-proven e2e registries-plus-validators contract and must keep its lifecycle/readiness model unchanged during extraction, with migrations limited to contract/config references. Recovery re-runs the verify-ladder and aggregate-confidence tests before promotion continues."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Governing meta-capability that defines the foundation's posture (semantic-first, evidence-backed, hermetically provable, AI-safe) and the lifecycle every other capability must honour rather than a CRUD service of its own. Its operational lifecycle is the V2 extraction lifecycle: each capability deploys a V1-proven contract and must keep its semanticCompleteness lifecycle/readiness model unchanged through extraction, with promotion only after the foundation matrix, registry, and validation checks pass. It owns no tenant records and is classified as a provider-dependency foundation concern whose health is the integrity of the foundation asset graph."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Governs the canonical relational store as a forward-only, numbered migration chain applied by a deterministic runner inside one transaction per file, recording each applied file with its content checksum so already-applied files become effectively immutable and corrections ship only as new forward migrations (never edits). Fresh installs apply the full chain in code-point order; an existing install skips checksum-matched files and applies only the new tail, so an existing install is already a current install at the data layer with zero data movement for prior files. The runner refuses to proceed on any checksum mismatch for an applied file, making the chain the load-bearing provenance and the data-verification gate."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Grant and revoke emit entitlement-granted and entitlement-revoked audit-before-change events, and a failing audit blocks persistence and leaves rows unchanged. Read-side evaluation is not audited as a mutation."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Grant emits a delegation-granted audit-before-change event whose failure prevents persistence, revoke emits a delegation-revoked event after a successful revoke, list emits a delegation-listed event on the authorised path, and no-op denied or not-found paths emit no audit. Grant audit precedes persistence."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Group lifecycle is list existing groups, create after name validation and a duplicate check, update after existence and conflict checks, and delete after a protected-name guard. Each mutation runs its precondition checks before touching the provider."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Group names must be non-empty strings of at most 64 characters with no path separators or control characters, must not be reserved, and must not duplicate an existing name case-insensitively. Invalid names are rejected before any provider write."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Heartbeats are operational telemetry and are not audit events; the auditable actions in this domain (operator redrive and related operations) are emitted by the event capability rather than by the worker. This keeps the worker's high-frequency liveness signal out of the privileged-action audit trail while still leaving redrive and operator actions auditable upstream."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Host identity follows a classify-then-resolve lifecycle: apex, reserved, invalid, and malformed hosts stay global with no tenant, tenant slug hosts resolve by organisation slug, active custom domains resolve through the domain registry, and inactive, pending, or disabled custom domains remain unresolved. Resolution is a pure per-request derivation feeding the request pipeline."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string
"Host resolution happens before authenticated user permissions exist; it produces tenant context rather than authorizing user action."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Host validation classifies apex, slug, local slug, reserved, unknown, malformed, host-with-port, and possible-custom-domain cases, and forwarded-host precedence is enforced deterministically. Custom domains must be verified and active to be accepted."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Import and export are tenant-scoped, security-sensitive operations that must preserve tenant isolation so a transfer cannot cross tenant boundaries. The operation is attributable and audited, and the durable progress record carries only tenant and digest keys rather than tenant content, limiting exposure. Permission, audit, and fail-closed behaviour are explicitly required to be preserved."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Import validates the archive digest to key progress and detect re-application, validates archive integrity (encrypted, well-formed) before applying, and records a failed unit rather than discarding it. Missing or invalid configuration fails closed; the progress record's tenant and digest keys are required to resume. Re-running the same archive is validated as idempotent against recorded completed units."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Incoming browser telemetry is validated for shape and required trace/correlation context before forwarding, and missing or invalid configuration fails closed instead of inventing defaults. Span and attribute names are kept within the controlled, OpenTelemetry-informed vocabulary so arbitrary client-supplied names are not accepted as canonical."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Ingestion records the event durably with subject/source/metadata so usage is attributable, and entitlement-gated rejection is observable. Audit/operational records precede or accompany the mutation rather than being reconstructed afterward."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Invalid create bodies fail closed with a validation error and permission denials are returned before handlers execute, so no partial catalog write occurs. Successful creates return the created entity with a creation status while list operations return the current set; provider failure degrades to a typed readiness failure rather than fabricating catalog state."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Invalid profile or preference bodies are rejected, an invalid tenant id is rejected, secret-bearing notification payloads are rejected before dispatch, disabled preferences suppress delivery, and a missing recipient fails rather than reporting a fake send. These invariants are exercised by the notification preference, dispatch, and transport runtime proofs so suppression and failure are explicit states, not silent drops."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Invalid role updates return an invalid-body outcome, missing memberships return not-found, and last-admin demotion, removal, or disable return explicit unprocessable-entity validation outcomes; permission denial is handled fail-closed by the request pipeline before any route handler runs. No partial role state is left on a rejected change."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Invalid, unknown, reserved, apex, and inactive/pending/disabled custom hosts resolve fail-closed to a null tenant context rather than to a partial or fallback tenant, and provider failure returns a typed degraded result without fabricating tenant state. No untrusted host is ever silently served as a tenant."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Invite, role change, username/status change, resend-invite, and remove emit audit only after validation and precondition reads, audit failure aborts the mutation, and conflict paths emit no misleading audit. Audit precedes the membership change."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Isolation checks are guard behaviour and do not emit mutation audit directly; audited mutations in tenant-scoped capabilities carry tenant/organisation metadata and fail before any cross-tenant write. The guard prevents the unsafe write before audit-bearing operations run."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Isolation readiness is proven by live substrate checks for the resolver, row-level security, storage prefixes, and tenant-scoped provider probes, with an unavailable provider treated as degraded/unreachable rather than isolated. Readiness reflects proven isolation, not assumed isolation."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"It owns no database schema of its own: service descriptors and readiness come from the catalog and from per-service readiness probes accessed through a readiness-probe port, with the capability holding a derived, tenant-scoped readiness record. Probe results are aggregated into discrete ready/degraded/blocked states per service, and behaviour changes update semantic artefacts rather than introducing owned tenant rows."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"It owns no database schema: durable storage lives in the metrics/trace backends (a Prometheus-style series store and an OTLP/Tempo-style trace store) reached through ports, while the capability holds only contract/config and a readiness record. Spans preserve tenant and request context as attributes for correlation, and behaviour changes must update the corresponding semantic artefacts rather than introducing an owned schema."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"It owns no database schema: RUM events and browser spans are emitted to a collection receiver and forwarded through a collector to the trace and log backends (e.g. Tempo and Loki), with only contract/config and a readiness record held locally. Trace context is propagated from the browser to the BFF so client and server spans join into one trace, and behaviour changes update semantic artefacts rather than introducing owned state."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"It owns no tenant records and exposes no tenant-mutating routes, so standard platform security controls apply; its tenant impact is indirect through correct posture labelling. Classification is an operator/governance concern, not an end-user permission. The separation it enforces is what prevents a hermetic or sandbox provider from being treated as production-live."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"It owns no tenant records and exposes no tenant-mutating routes, so standard platform security controls apply; its tenant impact is indirect through the isolation it enforces. The classification determines whether a service instance is shared across environments or isolated to one, which is an operator/governance concern rather than an end-user permission. Correct classification is what keeps environment boundaries from leaking."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Legal holds capture set-by and released-by actors with reason and lifecycle timestamps, providing a durable record of who protected what and why. Retention outcomes (pending, deleted, held) and residency rejections are observable per tenant through tenant-scoped error logs and route/use-case/provider spans that preserve tenant context. Recovery and restore must preserve audit and data-subject evidence alongside the data."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Lifecycle operations are explicit and ordered: provision creates the tenant, suspend coordinates data, storage, realm, then DSR after audit, and delete exports first and then coordinates storage, realm, DSR, and data. A coordinator sequences these subsystem transitions so destructive steps occur in a defined order."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"List routes require organisationId, invalid job ids are rejected, create validates the schedule body, run-now validates the job id, and the same-window idempotency window prevents duplicate event enqueue for a job that has already fired in the current window. Disabled jobs are never enqueued by the due tick. These invariants are exercised by the scheduled-jobs and scheduled-job-routes runtime proofs."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Local failure returns a typed platform error or a readiness-degraded state without changing tenant-visible semantics; there is no external provider to fabricate, so unavailable local dependencies fail closed through the readiness model. The risk class is semantic drift or configuration loss, not tenant data loss. A blocked ladder readiness or a failing promotion gate is an alertable foundation condition."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Local failure returns a typed platform error or a readiness-degraded state without changing tenant-visible semantics; there is no external provider to fabricate, so unavailable local dependencies fail closed through the readiness model. The risk class is semantic drift or configuration loss, not tenant data loss. A blocked or unavailable spine readiness is an alertable foundation condition."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Local failure returns a typed platform error or a readiness-degraded state without changing tenant-visible semantics; there is no external provider to fabricate, so unavailable local dependencies fail closed through the readiness model. The risk class is semantic drift or configuration loss, not tenant data loss. Blocked readiness, a failing promotion check, or repeated typed errors past threshold are alertable foundation conditions."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Local failure returns a typed platform error or a readiness-degraded state without changing tenant-visible semantics; unavailable local dependencies fail closed through the readiness model. An accessibility violation produces a failing gate verdict rather than a silent pass. The risk class is semantic drift or configuration loss, not tenant data loss."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Local failure returns a typed platform error or a readiness-degraded state without changing tenant-visible semantics; unavailable local dependencies fail closed through the readiness model. In strict mode a missing key or ungoverned raw literal produces a failing exit state rather than a silent default. The risk class is semantic drift or configuration loss, not tenant data loss."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Login and session creation are represented by authentication events and session-store state, and logout removes session state, while read-only session lookup and discovery validation carry no mutation audit. Every administrative mutation (provider create/update/delete/test, MFA, lockout, session, and claim-mapping changes) emits an audit-before-change event recording alias, operation, changed field names, and secret-changed booleans only; configuration and secret values are never audited, and audit failure aborts the mutation before the provider is touched."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Login sanitises the return-to target, emits PKCE challenge parameters, binds the callback to the pre-auth cookie, and rejects missing or unknown state/code and provider error callbacks while accepting only stored session cookies. Administrative validation enforces provider allowlists, required and safe-scheme OIDC URLs, reserved-alias rules, discovery issuer and JWKS validity (allowing plain HTTP only for local hosts), MFA enum values, positive lockout thresholds, bounded session lifespans, non-dangerous claim names, and realm roles restricted to the tenant-role allowlist; secrets are preserved when omitted on update and invalid bodies stop before any audit or provider mutation."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Maintains a data catalog with lineage, rules-based PII/sensitivity classification of datasets, and a data-subject-request workflow for privacy/GDPR fulfilment, composed from tenant foundation signals with audit. Classifications and request records progress through defined states, and request fulfilment captures durable evidence of what was done. The capability fails closed where source data or configuration is unavailable rather than inventing classifications or marking requests fulfilled without evidence."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Maintains an internal catalog of platform services and aggregates their readiness probes into a single tenant-scoped platform services readiness contract, so operators and tenant admins can see which composed services are ready. The capability is provider-backed and tenant-aware; it must keep its lifecycle/readiness model stable across extraction and preserve tenant isolation on what each tenant can observe."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Manages provider configurations through an explicit lifecycle (proposed, configured, ready, degraded, disabled) so each provider instance is declared, validated, and promoted deliberately; it is provider-backed and database-backed but owns no tenant records. It deploys the V1-proven contract for GET/POST /api/admin/provider-configs plus the per-id lifecycle and delete operations and must keep its lifecycle/readiness model unchanged during extraction. Recovery re-runs proof:provider-config and proof:provider-readiness-contract before promotion continues."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Membership lifecycle is explicit: an invite validates and creates either a pending invitation for a new user or a direct membership for an existing user, an invited membership becomes active on first login, role/status/username can be updated, a disabled membership can be re-enabled, and removal deletes the membership. Each transition is gated by precondition reads before any change."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Membership validation requires user id, organisation id, and a role and rejects system-admin as a tenant role, and permission resolution is proven to produce the correct bundles per role including the split between platform and tenant admin access. Unknown or invalid role values are rejected before any state change."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Meter-event ingestion is operator/internal and tenant-scoped, with usage reads available to the owning tenant and to operators for a specified tenant. Row-level isolation keys persistence by organisation so one tenant cannot read or write another tenant's usage; meter entitlement is enforced before an event is accepted."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Metrics and readiness operations are admin-gated under standard platform security controls; since no tenant rows are owned, isolation is enforced through scoped attributes (organisation/tenant id on signals and spans) rather than row-level data ownership. Access to the shared observability surface still fails closed when configuration or permission is missing."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Missing or unhealthy source data makes the ready flag false or fails the route/use case rather than producing a falsely-ready report. The report fails closed on absent sources and does not fabricate compliance posture."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string
