"Missing tenant context fails with a client error, missing API-access entitlement returns not-entitled, a revoked or invalid key authenticates to null, an invalid tenant identifier fails the operator rate-limit operation, and OpenAPI drift fails the architecture gates. Errors fail closed and never leak the secret or hash."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Mutations emit safe, metadata-only audit events for challenge creation, conflict rejection, verification, auth-client activation and deactivation, local routing proof, and canonical set and unset. Conflict paths in particular emit audit without ever including the DNS token, and audit precedes the corresponding state change."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"No client connects directly to the store; all data access is mediated through repository ports and adapters per the hexagonal constraint, with each bounded context exposing typed repository operations. The migration contract is forward-only with one transaction per file, code-point apply ordering, and a single secret-materialisation trust boundary that substitutes only the managed application-role password placeholder after rejecting quote, backslash, and control characters. New tenant-scoped tables MUST attach the canonical RLS predicate and the FORCE row-level-security setting as a contract obligation."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"No mutation audit applies because resolution is a read-only derivation; failed resolution is surfaced through resolver and pipeline warnings. There is no state change to audit."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Non-admin grant, list, and revoke attempts fail closed, a duplicate active grant short-circuits without mutation, the server overwrites client-supplied grantor with the caller's id, and tenant isolation keeps one organisation's grants from another. Invalid or unauthorised requests change no state."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Object lifecycle transitions (upload, scan outcome, quarantine, rejection) are recorded in the tenant-scoped registry, and operations preserve tenant context through spans with typed logs carrying the tenant/organisation identifier. Signed-URL issuance is bounded and attributable, and recovery must preserve tenant boundary, audit, and data-subject evidence. Quota changes are observable through the storage-bytes meter."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Objects are isolated by tenant prefix and by tenant-scoped registry access, so one tenant cannot enumerate or read another tenant's objects, and access to bytes is mediated by short-lived signed URLs rather than open buckets. The provider is identity-integrated so claim-to-policy mapping governs bucket access, and tenant-scoped registry rows enforce isolation in the database layer. Object operations are security-sensitive and must preserve permission and isolation."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Operations are tenant-scoped and audited through typed error logs carrying the tenant/organisation identifier and route/use-case/provider spans that preserve tenant context, while durable progress records make resumability and partial-failure state observable. The progress record intentionally excludes payload and secrets so the audit surface does not leak transported content. Recovery must preserve audit and data-subject evidence."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Operator catalog list and create operations require platform billing administration permission with read/write authorization; tenant catalog reads require a tenant billing-read permission and are scoped to the requesting organisation. Permission and entitlement checks run before any adapter call, and tenant context cannot read or mutate another tenant's catalog view."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Operator redrive emits an event.redriven audit record under audit-before-change semantics, so the audit write precedes the state mutation. Event publication and worker processing are captured as durable operational records and worker heartbeats rather than as user-mutation audit events, and redrive audit excludes the underlying payload. This separation keeps the operational telemetry distinct from the privileged-action audit trail."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Operator routes require platform delegation read/write permissions, grant is allowed for system-admin or tenant-admin contexts, revoke is system-admin only in current scope, and non-admin self-lookup is limited to the caller's own grantee id. Tenant isolation prevents one organisation's grants from appearing under another."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Operator routes validate tenant identifiers and the set-quota request schema; the use case treats absent quota as opt-in allowed, validates entitlement before any usage comparison, and evaluates deltas for usage-adding operations. The entitlement-before-usage ordering is a load-bearing invariant."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Outcomes are deterministic and fail closed: a duplicate publish is deduplicated, a handler that exhausts maxAttempts is dead-lettered, a missing organisationId returns 400, an invalid redrive id returns 400, and an unavailable Postgres substrate yields an honest skip or readiness failure rather than a fabricated success. Errors are typed and logged with organisationId when tenant-scoped, and no failure path echoes secret-bearing payload fields."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Outcomes are deterministic and fail closed: a handler error becomes a retry or, at maxAttempts, a dead-letter; an unavailable Postgres substrate causes an honest proof skip or readiness failure; and stale or stopped workers are explicit liveness states rather than hidden errors. Degraded mode disables the processing paths that depend on the Postgres adapter while keeping read-only readiness visible, and no path fabricates a processed result."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Outcomes are deterministic and fail closed: a missing organisationId returns 400, an invalid job id returns 400, a disabled job is simply not due, a repeated due tick within the window is deduplicated, and an unavailable Postgres substrate yields an honest skip or readiness failure rather than a fabricated enqueue. Errors are typed and tenant-scoped and never silently drop scheduled work."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Outcomes are deterministic and fail closed: a revoked, deleted, or cross-tenant ref resolves to null; an unreachable OpenBao reports degraded; an unavailable built-in Postgres degrades or skips honestly in proof; and no contract echoes a secret value on any failure path. Degraded mode disables the adapter-dependent mutation paths while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible, and no silent fallback upgrades provider readiness."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Outcomes are deterministic and fail closed: states include sent, suppressed, failed, readiness unavailable or degraded, no-tenant, validation error, invalid tenant id, and transport non-2xx failure, with each surfaced explicitly. Degraded mode disables the transport-dependent mutation and side-effect paths while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible. No failure path fabricates a successful send or echoes secret payload fields."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Outcomes are deterministic and fail-closed: invalid input maps to a validation error, unknown keys to not-found, non-overridable definitions to an unprocessable-entity outcome, insufficient permission to forbidden, and absence of tenant context to a bad-request; successful writes and deletes return no-content. Best-effort change-notification fan-out is decoupled and its failure never rolls back the committed configuration mutation."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Outcomes are typed and fail-closed as ok, not-found, not-verified, already-active, or not-active; a thrown auth-client port error leaves the registry inactive because the active marker is only written after the port call succeeds. Error handling therefore preserves the invariant that registry state matches external state."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Outcomes are typed and fail-closed as ok, not-found, not-verified, auth-client-inactive, or routing-not-proven, so each unmet precondition produces a distinct deterministic result rather than a partial change. The replacement of an existing canonical is atomic so the invariant cannot be transiently violated."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Outcomes are typed and fail-closed, including invalid-domain, domain-already-claimed, not-found, expired, already-verified, DNS-not-found, DNS-mismatch, not-verified, auth-client-inactive, routing-not-proven, and not-active alongside the success case. Conflict and failure paths never leak the DNS verification token, so error responses cannot expose ownership secrets."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Outcomes are typed and fail-closed, including no-credential, invalid-credential, forbidden-realm-operation, realm-unreachable, generic validation failure, not-found, and provider-specific readiness states. Failures never echo secret material in their messages, so error handling cannot become a secret-disclosure channel."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Paging inputs (limit, offset) are validated and bounded, and the projection enforces the safe-shape contract by emitting only the allowed summary fields. Tenant context is required so the read is correctly scoped. Missing or invalid configuration fails closed rather than returning an unscoped result."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Permissions are enforced only after tenant resolution; unresolved, apex, or reserved hosts grant no tenant context, tenant actors access only their own organisation's rows and prefixes, and operator bypass requires an explicit bypass/system role. Host identity is read-only and does not by itself grant data access."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Persisted state includes metric signals and metric samples, alert rules carrying comparator/threshold/severity, alert evaluation state (no-data, within, fired), incidents (open, acknowledged, resolved), and notification dispatch statuses (sent, suppressed), all under tenant row-level-security boundaries. State evolution uses ordered, forward-only migrations that preserve the proven alert/incident state machine and cannot silently drop or remap records."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Persisted state includes per-service descriptors (id, resource, apex path, tenant path, classification), a landing path, a dev-only flag, and the system-admin and tenant-admin resource sets, from which an access decision (granted plus reason) and a clickthrough URL are derived. State evolves through ordered, forward-only migrations that preserve the proven policy/decision model and cannot silently drop or remap tenant access rules."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Persisted state is log entries keyed by low-cardinality service and level labels, with high-cardinality identifiers (organisation/tenant id, request id, trace id) carried as structured fields rather than labels to control series cardinality. Backing the entries is a readiness record exposing the discrete states log ingestion, tenant-scoped query, trace correlation, dashboards, collector, metrics, and error capture; schema evolution uses ordered, forward-only migrations that preserve tenant rows and audit lineage."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Persistent state is the platform_events table partitioned by organisationId, holding eventType, idempotencyKey, payload, status in pending|processing|processed|dead_letter, and attempts against maxAttempts, alongside worker_heartbeats recording alive|stale|stopped liveness. Dead-letter records retain tenant, event type, attempt count, a payload summary, and the last error so redrive can reconstruct context; ordering is guaranteed per organisation and idempotency key with no cross-tenant ordering guarantee. Row-level security scopes every read and mutation to the owning organisation."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Policy denial maps to 403, insufficient auth level maps to a step-up-required/401, a missing expected token maps to authentication-required/401, and static fallback without a permission maps to 403; every path is fail-closed by default. Server unavailability is an explicit non-decisive degradation, not an implicit allow."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Policy state consists of policy key, entitlement key, limit, window seconds, action, and updated-at/updated-by; counter state is per tenant, policy, and window with a used count and an exceeded state once the used count passes the limit. Counters are bucketed by window and reset on a new bucket rather than being decremented."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Preference changes and operator test sends are audit-before-change or audit-before-action operations, so the audit record precedes the effect. Dispatch records a durable per-attempt status (sent, suppressed, or failed), and the audit metadata deliberately excludes secret-bearing payload content. This separates auditable operator and user actions from the durable delivery log."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Profile and preferences are always-on once the data substrate is migrated, and degraded mode disables store-dependent writes while keeping read-only access and audit visible. Live proofs skip honestly when the substrate is unavailable and verify no secret columns plus tenant-isolation enforcement."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Profile lifecycle moves from a default to an updated own-profile record, and preference lifecycle moves from default-empty to updated channel/category preferences that are read back; notification dispatch then treats enabled preferences as sent and disabled preferences as suppressed. All operations act only on the authenticated subject's own data."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Profile update rejects an empty display name, the route schema rejects invalid profile or preference payloads, dispatch rejects secret-bearing payload fields, and a write without tenant context returns a no-tenant error. Invalid input is rejected before any change."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Profile updates emit a profile-updated audit-before-change event, preference updates emit a preference audit, and operator test sends emit a notification-tested event. Audit precedes the change."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Proof for this capability is the foundation matrix plus the registry and validation test that demonstrate the corpus is internally consistent and that each capability's claims are backed by evidence, not assertion. Historical demonstration is via that hermetic foundation tooling rather than live external runtime. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Proof is proof:provider-environment-classification, demonstrating that the matrix keeps provider mode and environment as separate, honestly classified dimensions. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Proof is the build-versus-compose decision framework document and its associated checks, demonstrating the criteria are applied consistently across the capability set; it is a foundation-document proof rather than a runtime probe. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Proof is the environment-service-classification document and associated checks demonstrating consistent shared-versus-environment-specific classification; it is a foundation-document proof rather than a live runtime probe. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Proof is the verify-ladder and aggregate-confidence test suites that demonstrate the ladder gates promotion per stage without inflating proof posture. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provider failure returns a typed degraded/readiness failure and never fabricates successful provider state; repeated typed errors crossing a threshold are an explicit alert condition. Because the capability owns no tenant data, the dominant failure risk is semantic drift or configuration loss rather than data loss, and error paths keep mutation boundaries closed."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provider failure returns a typed degraded/readiness failure rather than fabricating evaluation results, and repeated typed errors crossing a threshold are an explicit alert condition. Illegal incident transitions and invalid rule mutations are rejected deterministically, keeping mutation boundaries closed; the dominant risk is semantic/config drift since no tenant records are owned."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provider failure returns a typed degraded/readiness failure, keeps mutation boundaries closed, and does not fabricate successful provider state; degraded mode disables dependent side-effect paths while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible. The risk class is semantic drift or configuration loss, not tenant data loss. A blocked classification readiness or failing promotion proof is alertable."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provider failure returns a typed degraded/readiness failure, keeps mutation boundaries closed, and does not fabricate successful provider state; degraded mode disables dependent side-effect paths while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible. The risk class is semantic drift or configuration loss, not tenant data loss. Blocked readiness or a failing promotion proof is alertable."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provider failure returns a typed degraded/readiness failure, keeps mutation boundaries closed, and does not fabricate successful provider state; degraded mode disables side-effect paths that depend on the HTTP health-probe adapter while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible. The risk class is semantic drift or configuration loss rather than tenant data loss. A failed health probe moves the provider to degraded rather than reporting false readiness."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provider failure returns a typed degraded/readiness failure, keeps mutation boundaries closed, and does not fabricate successful provider state; degraded mode disables side-effect paths that depend on the manifest-env adapter while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible. The risk class is semantic drift or configuration loss, not tenant data loss. A failed bootstrap or blocked readiness is an alertable provider-dependency condition."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provider failure returns a typed degraded/readiness failure, keeps mutation boundaries closed, and does not fabricate successful provider state; degraded mode disables side-effecting paths that depend on the observability adapters while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible. Tenant data loss is possible only if migration, restore, or export semantics are bypassed, which the error model forbids. A missing tenant isolation or audit signal is an alertable tenant-data-or-security condition."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provider failure returns a typed degraded/readiness failure, keeps mutation boundaries closed, and never fabricates a successful provider result. Duplicate charge submissions resolve to the same outcome via the idempotency key, and a failed capture does not silently advance subscription or invoice state."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provider or pipeline failure returns a typed degraded/readiness failure and never fabricates a successful collection or trace; repeated typed errors crossing a threshold are an explicit alert condition. The capability owns no tenant data, so the dominant failure risk is semantic drift or configuration loss, and mutation boundaries stay closed under failure."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provider or reconciler failure returns a typed degraded/readiness failure and keeps mutation boundaries closed, never fabricating a granted decision or a successful reconciliation. Because access is tenant-affecting, a denied or indeterminate decision defaults to no access, and tenant data/policy loss is possible only if migration/restore semantics are bypassed."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provider-config operations are administrative endpoints; the plane owns no tenant data, so standard platform security controls govern access rather than per-tenant roles. Credential references are gated by requiresCredential and resolved through the secrets boundary rather than exposed in config reads. Mutating the lifecycle of a provider is an operator action that must keep mutation boundaries closed on failure."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provides a built-in alerting and incident lifecycle over the platform's own signals: it registers metric signals, evaluates alert rules against samples, raises incidents, and bridges fired alerts to notification dispatch via an observability signals / alerts / incidents / readiness contract. The capability is provider- and database-backed but owns no tenant records, and its lifecycle/readiness model must be preserved across extraction."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provides a metrics query operation and a readiness query behind ports/adapters so the metrics and trace providers (e.g. Prometheus and an OTel collector feeding Tempo) are swappable without changing the contract. The emitted metric names follow a stable per-capability convention (request total, failure total, readiness state) and traces expose route/use-case/provider spans that carry tenant context end to end."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provides a paired tenant data export and import flow with portability integrity, producing an encrypted compressed archive on export and applying it on import through a Postgres applier, with durable resumable progress so a failed transfer can resume rather than restart. The overriding invariant is that a failed transfer must never cause silent data loss. Import progress is persisted so partial work survives interruption."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provides a read-only projection of tenant and admin history assembled from audit and related sources, exposed through tenant-history and admin-tenant-history reads; it is strictly a query surface and performs no mutation. Entries are projected from underlying records into a safe summarised shape on read. The projection deliberately excludes sensitive raw material so history can be browsed without exposing secrets."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provides point-in-time recovery drills, per-resource retention windows, legal holds that block deletion, and single-region data-residency tagging over tenant data, exposed through administrative data operations. A retention worker periodically evaluates expired candidates and deletes or anonymises them UNLESS an active legal hold protects the resource; legal holds move from active to released and residency tags are owned on the tenant record. The whole capability fails closed where source data or configuration is unavailable so that retention never destroys protected or unverified data."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provides runtime internationalisation with locale resolution plus a validation gate that ensures required keys exist and raw literals are governed, treating UI strings as contractual; it is database-backed in lineage but owns no tenant records. It deploys the V1-proven packages/i18n-runtime contract and must keep its lifecycle/readiness model unchanged during extraction, with the validation gate run as a build/promotion check. Recovery re-runs the i18n-runtime package and its validation before promotion continues."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provides tenant object storage with per-tenant key prefixes, signed-URL access, and an upload-scan lifecycle, exposed through object, readiness, and probe operations; object bytes live in the object-storage provider while a per-object registry row tracks lifecycle in the relational store. An object moves through scan states from uploaded to clean, quarantined, or rejected, and storage usage is metered. The capability composes an object-storage adapter with a relational object-registry repository."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Provides tenant product search backed by full-text indexing with a reindex path and a readiness probe, exposed through tenant search and admin search readiness and reindex operations; documents are indexed into a tenant-scoped relational full-text store and queried with permission gating. Indexed documents are kept in sync with their sources and can be rebuilt via reindex. The search engine is a full-text-search adapter behind a port, with alternative engines available as future provider adapters."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Publish rejects payload fields that carry secrets, preserves the tenant id, and deduplicates repeated idempotency keys; list routes require organisationId and return 400 when it is missing, and redrive rejects an invalid or unknown event id with 400. Row-level security additionally hides foreign-tenant events so validation cannot be bypassed by id guessing. Invariants are exercised by the event-bus and event-redrive runtime proofs."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Put returns no value, list and getMetadata are value-free, resolve is the only value-returning server path, rotation preserves the opaque ref while incrementing the version, OpenBao stores the value outside Postgres, and readiness payloads contain no secret-bearing fields. These invariants are exercised by the secret-store contract and OpenBao proofs to guarantee values never leak through metadata or readiness surfaces."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"put, revoke, and delete emit audit-before-change records carrying only name, ref, and provider metadata and never the value, so the audit write precedes the store mutation. Where the use-case wraps the store write, an audit failure prevents the mutation, making audit a hard precondition for change. This guarantees a complete, value-free audit trail for every secret-lifecycle action."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Queries are validated and scoped to the tenant and, where present, the permission key, so unscoped or cross-tenant queries are rejected; indexing validates the document shape and uniqueness on tenant/type/document id. Readiness is validated by a probe reporting ready, degraded, or blocked. Missing or invalid configuration fails closed rather than returning unscoped results."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Query parameters are validated for type, range, and required scope before being passed to a provider, and missing or invalid configuration fails closed instead of inventing defaults. Invariants ensure metric and span emission stays within the declared, controlled vocabulary so arbitrary metric or attribute names are not silently accepted."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness classifies no-subscriptions, configured, and has-dead-deliveries, while worker and redrive proofs validate pending/dead/delivered metrics against live relational storage. When the webhook adapter or delivery worker is unavailable, mutation/side-effect paths are disabled and read-only readiness and audit remain visible."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness combines hermetic in-memory or local workflow-closure validation, the Temporal provider adapter and its live proof, and a dedicated workflow readiness route; the live provider proof skips honestly when its endpoints are unavailable. Provider failure degrades readiness explicitly and never upgrades hermetic closure to a live-provider claim. Closure is level-3 hermetic state-machine validation; live provider validation is level-4 when the workflow-provider profile is available."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness combines operator visibility of the event and dead-letter queues with worker heartbeat liveness (alive|stale|stopped); it degrades explicitly and disables mutation/side-effect paths that depend on the Postgres adapter while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible. Live proofs fail closed on row-level-security, secret-payload, retry, redrive, or heartbeat regressions and skip honestly when Postgres is unavailable, so production-shaped readiness is never reported as production-live."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness covers local canonical cutover only; public DNS and TLS are explicitly deferred, and canonical is treated as a marker that does not imply public routing or TLS readiness. The capability therefore degrades honestly to a local-only posture when external infrastructure is unavailable."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness depends on both the object-storage adapter and the relational object-registry repository being reachable; a probe verifies the provider, and the capability degrades explicitly when either is unavailable, disabling mutating storage paths while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible. Readiness being blocked, a failed tenant-storage-objects proof during promotion, or a missing isolation or audit signal raise alerts and block promotion."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness depends on the archive builder and the Postgres import applier being available; the capability degrades explicitly when those adapters are unavailable, disabling the transfer path while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible. Readiness being blocked, a failed portability proof during promotion, or a missing isolation or audit signal raise alerts and block promotion."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness depends on the governance adapter and its store being reachable; the capability degrades explicitly when the adapter is unavailable, disabling mutating governance paths while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible. Readiness being blocked, a failed governance proof during promotion, or a missing isolation or audit signal raise alerts and block promotion."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness depends on the substrate being reachable and fully migrated; the migrated check (a non-empty migration ledger) and the cross-tenant isolation live-proof (an unfiltered count under a foreign tenant context returning zero) are the acceptance gates. When the substrate is unavailable the capability degrades explicitly, disabling mutation and side-effect paths while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible rather than failing silently. Promotion is blocked when readiness is unavailable or when the isolation or audit signal is missing."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness depends on the underlying audit/history store being reachable; the capability degrades explicitly when that substrate is unavailable, keeping read-only readiness and audit visible (it has no mutation path to disable). Readiness being blocked, a failed history proof during promotion, or a missing isolation or audit signal raise alerts and block promotion."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness distinguishes built-in Postgres ready, OpenBao ready, and OpenBao degraded or unreachable, and emits secret-free readiness payloads; the built-in check is a Postgres SELECT 1 and the OpenBao check is its sys/health endpoint, and an OpenBao outage yields degraded rather than a fabricated ready. No silent fallback upgrades provider readiness, so a hermetic or composed state is never reported as a live-external-provider state."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness distinguishes no-domains, pending-DNS, verified, inactive auth-client, locally-routed, deferred public DNS/TLS, and canonical redirect cutover states. Local proofs explicitly decline to claim public DNS or TLS readiness, so the capability degrades honestly to a local-only posture when external infrastructure is absent."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness for the live session path depends on identity-provider, session-store, and configuration availability, with an explicit deterministic fixture mode for tests; administrative readiness is credential-derived and only reports configured/ok when the tenant realm credential can read and mutate policies, otherwise classifying missing-credential, invalid-credential, forbidden-realm-operation, realm-unreachable, or discovery-invalid rather than hiding them. Degraded mode disables provider-dependent mutation paths while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible, and real brokered/interactive IdP login is carried as externally limited rather than fake-passed."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is a first-class, queryable posture reporting the discrete sub-states (log ingestion, tenant-scoped query, trace correlation, dashboards, collector, metrics, error capture) and degrades explicitly when the search adapter or substrate is unavailable. In degraded mode mutation/side-effect paths that depend on the search adapter are disabled while read-only readiness and audit visibility are retained; emitted readiness, error, and audit signals use the controlled, OpenTelemetry-informed observability vocabulary."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is a queryable posture covering metrics and trace pipelines that degrades explicitly when the metrics provider or OTel collector is unavailable, disabling dependent side-effect paths while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible. Emitted readiness, error, and audit signals use the controlled, OpenTelemetry-informed observability vocabulary without claiming OpenTelemetry compliance."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is a queryable posture spanning signal ingestion, alert evaluation, and incident/notification wiring that degrades explicitly when the underlying providers are unavailable, disabling dependent side-effect paths while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible. Emitted readiness, error, and audit signals use the controlled, OpenTelemetry-informed observability vocabulary."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is always-on once the data substrate is migrated, and degraded mode disables store-dependent mutation while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible. Live proofs skip honestly when the substrate is unavailable and never fake-pass."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is assembled from live foundation signals and route registration, with the report's ready flag true only when the required source readiness values satisfy the use case. Composition is deterministic so the same inputs produce the same readiness verdict."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is encoded directly in lifecycleState: a provider is ready only after it is configured, credentialed where required, and health-probed, and it degrades explicitly when the probe or substrate is unavailable. Readiness fails closed and stays visible read-only in degraded mode. Promotion is gated on proof:provider-config and proof:provider-readiness-contract passing."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is gate success plus optional security-console/service readiness from platform service probes, with missing local tools classified honestly according to each script's mode. Readiness fails closed on missing or stale evidence rather than assuming success."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is gated on the retention worker, legal-hold store, and residency enforcement being reachable and on the restore drill succeeding; the capability degrades explicitly when its adapters or the residency column are unavailable, keeping read-only readiness and audit visible while disabling the deletion path. Readiness being blocked, a failed restore/retention/legal-hold/residency proof during promotion, or a missing isolation or audit signal raise alerts and block promotion."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is hermetic-domain ready for approval and support-session semantics, with the workflow waiting for an approval signal and completing on approval, and no live external provider is claimed. Degraded mode disables provider-dependent paths while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is invariant-ready because permission resolution is a pure, fully-tested function and route enforcement is exercised through pipeline permission tests; degraded mode disables store-dependent mutation while keeping read-only resolution available. There is no external provider dependency for resolution itself."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is invariant-ready for contextual audit reads, and degraded mode keeps read-only projection visible while disabling any dependent mutation. A broader live history proof validates read-only projection, source isolation, secret exclusion, pagination, and absence of mutation against the live data substrate."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is invariant-ready for the local policy seam, and authorization-server unavailability and resource-not-registered are explicit degraded, non-decisive states with a static fallback rather than a fake allow. Degraded mode keeps read-only readiness and audit visible."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is invariant-ready for the usecase contract, local runtime proof exercises the composition root against in-memory port and audit, and storage behaviour is covered by adapter tests; degraded mode disables store-dependent mutation while keeping read-only listing and audit visible."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is invariant-ready once tenant context and the identity store are available, with an admin-count readiness signal, and degraded mode disables store-dependent mutation while keeping read-only listing and audit visible. Pending-invitation queries always filter by organisation id."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is invariant-ready once the organisations table is available; because that table has no row-level security, every query explicitly filters by the parent id from the resolved tenant context, and degraded mode disables store-dependent mutation while keeping read-only listing visible."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is invariant-ready once the resolver and domain registry are available, and degraded mode disables registry-dependent mutation while keeping read-only resolution and audit visible. Live proofs skip honestly when seeded local substrate is absent rather than faking tenant resolution."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is invariant-ready when resolver code and the domain registry are available, and degraded mode disables registry-dependent paths while keeping read-only resolution visible. Runtime proof needs local substrate for live resolution and skips honestly when no seeded organisation exists."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is live route/use-case availability over relational support tables and metering-derived health signals, with the support-approval proof validating the workflow boundary state rather than assuming support access. Degraded mode disables mutation paths while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is migration- and catalog-seed-backed: route-registration evidence validates the exposed surface and unit behaviour validates in-process catalog operations, while live provider billing readiness is tracked as a separate capability. When the catalog adapter is unavailable, mutation paths are disabled and only read-only readiness and audit remain visible."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is proven against live relational storage covering idempotent insertion, the entitlement gate, aggregation, and row-level tenant isolation with no secret columns; route handlers and access-control metadata are validated separately. When the metering substrate is unavailable, mutation paths are disabled and readiness degrades explicitly."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is proven against live storage covering entitlement-before-quota ordering, the exceeded state, typed denial via assert, revoke-driven denial, and the no-quota allow path, with route handlers validated separately. When the quota substrate is unavailable, mutation paths are disabled and readiness degrades explicitly."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is reported by the full-text engine probe as ready, degraded, or blocked, and is verified by isolation and route proofs; the capability degrades explicitly when the search adapter is unavailable, disabling index mutation while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible. Readiness being blocked, a failed search/search-isolation/search-routes proof during promotion, or a missing isolation or audit signal raise alerts and block promotion."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is that the due tick is invocable and the routes are accessible, even though the continuous daemon loop is not claimed; the live proof validates the table schema, row-level-security isolation, due/run-now enqueue behaviour, and the route handlers, and degrades explicitly when the substrate is unavailable. Because dispatch rides the event substrate, scheduled-job readiness inherits the event-bus degraded posture and never reports production-shaped behaviour as production-live."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is the aggregate honesty of the foundation: a capability is ready only when its V1-proven contract, migration lineage, and proof inventory are intact and the matrix/registry/validation checks pass. Readiness fails closed when evidence is missing, stale, or unknown, and degraded mode keeps read-only readiness and audit visible. Promotion is gated on re-running the foundation matrix, registry, and validation after any fix."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is the capability's primary output: it aggregates per-service probes into a tenant-scoped posture that degrades explicitly when a probe, provider, or substrate is unavailable, keeping read-only readiness and audit visible while disabling dependent side-effect paths. Emitted readiness, error, and audit signals use the controlled, OpenTelemetry-informed observability vocabulary."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is the stage-aware verdict itself: a capability may advance only when its current stage's confidence threshold is met, and the ladder degrades explicitly rather than upgrading posture by implication. It fails closed on missing, stale, or unknown stage evidence. Promotion is gated on the verify-ladder and aggregate-confidence checks passing."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is the strict drift gate passing with zero missing routes, zero extra routes, zero unresolved references, and zero schemaless bodies. Any nonzero drift blocks readiness rather than producing a warning that can be ignored."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is this capability's whole purpose: it reports overall composed-provider readiness and degrades explicitly when any required provider or the substrate is unavailable, never upgrading readiness by implication. It fails closed on missing, stale, or unknown inputs. Promotion is gated on proof:composed-provider-readiness passing."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness is worker heartbeat liveness (alive|stale|stopped) together with the event-processing proof; a failure to claim, process, or dead-letter is a proof and readiness failure rather than a silent stall. Readiness degrades explicitly when the substrate is unavailable and never upgrades a production-shaped state to production-live. Liveness states are surfaced rather than masked so stale or stopped workers are visible to operators."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness means each in-scope capability has an explicit, current, justified disposition and no capability is silently undecided; unavailable dependencies fail closed through the readiness model. Readiness is demonstrated by re-running the framework document and named proof rather than by a live service heartbeat. Stale or unknown decisions do not count as ready."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness means every relevant provider has an explicit, consistent environment classification with provider mode and environment kept separate; unavailable dependencies fail closed through the readiness model. Readiness is shown by re-running proof:provider-environment-classification rather than a live heartbeat. Stale or unknown classifications do not count as ready."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness means every service's environment classification is present, consistent, and enforced, and the routing/isolation it implies resolves; unavailable dependencies fail closed through the readiness model. Readiness is shown by re-running the environment-service-classification document and named proof. Stale or unknown classifications do not count as ready."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness means the audited UI surfaces meet the accessibility expectations and the e2e accessibility spec passes; unavailable dependencies fail closed through the readiness model. Readiness is demonstrated by re-running the accessibility spec rather than by a live heartbeat. Missing, stale, or unknown results do not count as ready."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness means the locale corpus passes the validation gate (required keys present, interpolation consistent, raw literals governed) for the configured strictness; unavailable dependencies fail closed through the readiness model. Readiness is demonstrated by re-running validate-i18n and the i18n-runtime tests. A report-only pass with outstanding strict findings is not full readiness."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness queries and catalog interactions are correlated to request and trace identifiers, and any state-affecting catalog action is recorded as an auditable event preserving tenant boundary and DSR/GDPR evidence. A missing tenant-isolation or audit signal on this surface is itself an alert condition."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness reflects billing-provider availability: the in-memory adapter supports hermetic validation while the external adapter classifies live provider availability, degrading explicitly when the provider is unreachable. Degraded mode disables provider-dependent mutation paths while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness reflects whether each service's providers resolve and its catalog entry is coherent; it degrades explicitly when the underlying substrate (for example the observability adapters) is unavailable rather than reporting false health. Readiness fails closed and remains visible read-only in degraded mode. Promotion is gated on the named platform-services and catalog proofs passing."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness reflects whether environments are registered and bootstrap can deterministically produce valid configuration; it degrades explicitly when the manifest-env substrate is unavailable rather than reporting false health. Readiness fails closed and stays visible read-only in degraded mode. Promotion is gated on the environment-registry, admin-bootstrap, and operations proofs passing."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness reflects whether policy derivation and proxy reconciliation are healthy and degrades explicitly when the reconciler or substrate is unavailable, disabling reconciliation side-effects while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible. Emitted readiness, error, and audit signals use the controlled, OpenTelemetry-informed observability vocabulary."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness reflects whether the backup path can produce a valid artifact in the current environment under its guard; when the dump or restore tooling is unavailable the capability degrades, disabling the destructive path while keeping read-only readiness visible. Readiness being blocked, a failed backup proof during promotion, or repeated typed errors over threshold raise alerts. Restore is never part of normal readiness flow because it is destructive and confirmation-gated."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness reflects whether the RUM SDK, collection receiver, collector, and downstream trace/log backends are wired and healthy, degrading explicitly when any stage is unavailable while keeping read-only readiness and audit visible. Emitted readiness, error, and audit signals use the controlled, OpenTelemetry-informed observability vocabulary without claiming OpenTelemetry compliance."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness reports configured, missing, invalid, forbidden, unreachable, or provider-unavailable states without exposing any secret material, and provider-backed secret stores require live substrate validation to be considered ready. The capability degrades to an explicit not-ready classification rather than assuming availability."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Readiness reports the real availability of the local, SMTP, and webhook transports; the Mailpit and webhook proofs skip honestly when their backing services are absent and never mark a fake send as sent. Because this is a tenant-data capability, readiness must also preserve tenant isolation and audit signals, and a missing isolation or audit signal is an alert condition. Provider failure degrades readiness explicitly rather than upgrading a composed or production-shaped state to production-live."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Reads are tenant-scoped so a tenant sees only its own history, while the admin variant is operator-scoped to read a named tenant's history under privileged access; both preserve tenant isolation. Because the projection omits payloads, tokens, and secrets, even authorised readers cannot extract sensitive material through history. Access flows through ports and adapters, never a direct client database connection."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Reads require a tenant-scoped configuration-read permission and additionally filter the visible definitions by each definition's required read permission; mutations require a tenant-scoped configuration-write permission and the use case re-enforces each definition's required write permission. Feature-flag definitions require dedicated feature permissions, and all resolution is tenant-isolated so one tenant never observes another tenant's overrides."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Reads use a self-read permission and writes use a self-update permission, with the user id always taken from the authenticated session subject and never from a path or body parameter. The separate operator notification test uses platform notification permissions outside this self-service surface, preserving isolation."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Registers environments and bootstraps their configuration, turning declared manifests into generated environment configuration; it is provider-backed but owns no tenant records. It deploys the V1-proven contract manifests-to-generated-.env and must keep its lifecycle/readiness model unchanged during extraction, with migrations limited to contract/config references that update semantic artefacts when behaviour changes. Recovery re-runs proof:environment-registry, proof:environment-admin-bootstrap, and proof:environment-operations before promotion continues."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Registers platform services and their provider integration model, governing how each service is built, composed, or adapted and how it is exposed; it is provider-backed, database-backed, and touches tenant data. It deploys the V1-proven contract for platform-services readiness and GET /api/platform/service-catalog (catalog v2) and must keep its lifecycle/readiness model unchanged during extraction. Recovery re-runs proof:platform-services, proof:service-clickthrough-policy, proof:service-catalog-registry, and proof:entitlements-routes before promotion continues."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Report reads are not mutation audits; review and compliance-completion actions are audited by their owning workflows and source audit rows. The report composes existing audited signals rather than emitting new mutation audit."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Requests are validated for required tenant scope and well-formed service references before probes are invoked, and missing or invalid configuration fails closed instead of inventing default readiness. Aggregation invariants ensure a service with an unknown or failed probe is reported as not-ready rather than silently omitted."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Resource-policy mutations emit an audit-before-change event and audit failure prevents the adapter mutation, while read-only authorization checks are logged or returned rather than audited per request. Audit precedes any policy change."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Retention evaluation validates the configured window and filter and, critically, checks for an active legal hold before treating any candidate as deletable. Legal-hold operations validate actor and reason; residency placement validates the target region against the tenant's home tag and rejects mismatches. Point-in-time recovery is validated by a restore drill rather than assumed."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Retention policies are tenant-scoped rows naming a target resource class, a time-to-live window, an apply filter (all rows or by status), and an enabled flag; each retention candidate resolves to an outcome of pending, deleted, or held. Legal holds are tenant-scoped records with active or released state plus reason, set-by and released-by actors, and set and released timestamps, where active is defined by an unset release timestamp; the held-row invariant is that an active hold on a resource blocks its retention deletion. Data residency is a single-region tag owned by the tenant/organisation row, and placement enforcement rejects writes targeting a non-home region."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Role and status mutations emit audit events, and audit failure aborts the role change before the underlying store is mutated. Pure read-side permission resolution is not itself audited."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Routes are global, operator-only platform surfaces: reading the event list and the dead-letter list requires platform.events.read, redrive requires platform.events.write, and worker listing requires platform.workers.read. Tenant isolation is enforced by organisationId partitioning plus row-level security so one organisation can never observe or redrive another organisation's events, and list routes require an explicit organisationId. Secrets and provider credentials never cross the event boundary."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Routes declare an explicit required permission, resource, and scope consumed as a policy-enforcement point, and resource-policy writes sit behind tenant auth-settings permission with audit-before-adapter mutation. Authorization itself is the permission gate for every protected operation."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Routes enforce explicit required permissions such as tenant.members.*, tenant.groups.*, tenant.suborgs.*, and platform.* and never the role name directly, with platform.admin.access kept distinct from tenant.admin.access. Permission resolution is tenant-scoped so a tenant role only yields that tenant's permissions."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Routes require the specific group read, create, update, or delete permission, are tenant-scoped, and declare a group resource and matching scopes, resolving the tenant realm credential from context. One tenant cannot manage another tenant's groups."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Routes require the specific member read, invite, update-role, or delete permission, and the manager role intentionally holds only a legacy member bundle without the tenant member-management permissions. All reads and writes derive the tenant from resolved context, never from client input, preserving tenant isolation."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Routes require the specific sub-organisation read, create, update, or delete permission, are tenant-scoped, and declare a sub-organisation resource and matching scopes. Tenant isolation is enforced by filtering on the resolved parent id."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Runtime domain-identity matrix and custom-domain resolution proofs validate live local resolver behaviour across all host classes, demonstrated in source lineage via hermetic/runtime substrate validation. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Runtime readiness is the tenant-lifecycle proof, which validates audit-first behaviour and the subsystem coordination order for suspend and delete. Readiness degrades explicitly when the lifecycle coordinator substrate is unavailable."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"scheduled_job.set and scheduled_job.run are audit-before-change operations, so the audit record is written before the schedule mutation or manual run takes effect. The recurring due-tick enqueue is represented operationally by the resulting platform_events records rather than as a separate user-mutation audit event. This keeps operator intent auditable while treating routine dispatch as operational telemetry."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Scheduled-job routes are global, operator-only platform surfaces: listing requires platform.jobs.read while create, run-now, and patch require platform.jobs.write. The due tick is server-internal and is not callable from tenant UI. Tenant isolation is enforced by organisationId scoping and row-level security so one organisation cannot list or trigger another organisation's jobs."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Search and readiness operations are admin-gated and hard-bound to a single tenant: every query is scoped to the caller's organisation id so one tenant can never read another tenant's log entries. Permission, audit, and fail-closed checks are treated as security-sensitive invariants that must survive extraction unchanged, and missing tenant context fails the request rather than widening scope."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Search and reindex operations preserve tenant context through route/use-case/provider spans, with typed error logs carrying the tenant/organisation identifier when tenant-scoped, and readiness transitions are observable as a signal. Indexed metadata excludes secrets so audit and logs do not surface sensitive content. Recovery must preserve tenant boundary and audit."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Search inputs (time range, label/field filters, tenant scope) are validated for type and bounds before execution, and the mandatory tenant scope is asserted so an unscoped or cross-tenant query is rejected rather than broadened. Invariants are enforced ahead of any provider call so malformed input cannot reach the log store or leak entries outside the tenant boundary."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Search results are isolated by tenant under the canonical row-level-security predicate and further gated by an optional per-document permission key so a user only sees documents they are entitled to, never another tenant's documents. Admin readiness and reindex are operator-scoped privileged operations. Indexed metadata deliberately omits secret fields so the search surface cannot leak sensitive values."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Secret writes are governed by the permissions of the owning surface (such as auth-settings write, provider-config permissions, webhook write, and API-key create/revoke scopes), and reads return only redacted metadata. Secrets are tenant-scoped through their owning resource, and there is no permission that grants retrieval of a stored raw secret."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Secret-bearing settings follow a write-only lifecycle: callers create, rotate, or update a secret, the value is validated before storage where applicable, then stored encrypted, hashed, or provider-masked, after which only non-sensitive metadata such as a has-secret flag and readiness is exposed. A blank or absent secret on update preserves the existing value, and clearing occurs only through the owning resource's lifecycle rather than via a raw-read path."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Secrets are validated before storage or provider mutation, unsafe URLs or configurations are rejected, invalid tenant credentials are classified before any store occurs, an empty identity-provider secret preserves the existing value, and encryption-key requirements are enforced for higher environments. Validation therefore runs ahead of any secret-bearing side effect."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Self-service preference reads and writes use profile.read_self and profile.update_self with tenant context derived from the request host, while operator readiness and test-send routes are global and require platform.notifications.read or platform.notifications.write. A user can therefore manage only their own preferences, and operator test sends are gated behind operator permissions. Tenant isolation must be preserved because the capability holds tenant-visible data."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Semantic readiness is invariant-ready, while route execution additionally requires tenant context and the tenant-realm auth-settings credential, and degraded mode disables provider-dependent mutation while keeping read-only readiness visible. A UI semantic harness proves the generation contract without shipping a legacy page."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Service descriptors, classification, and resource-set membership are validated before a decision is derived, and missing or invalid configuration fails closed rather than granting access by default. The dev-only flag and tenant/path bindings are checked so a malformed or out-of-context request cannot produce an over-broad clickthrough URL."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Set and unset emit canonical set and unset audit events carrying domain and redirect-policy metadata before the registry mutation. Audit precedes the state change so every canonical transition is recorded ahead of being applied."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Setting a quota emits an audit record before the mutation (audit-before-upsert) carrying the acting operator, and denial decisions are observable for enforcement. The quota resource is identified explicitly in audit metadata."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Setting a rate-limit policy emits an audit record before the mutation (audit-before-change) with the rate-limit resource identified, so policy changes are attributable. Evaluation decisions are observable for enforcement."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Setting canonical requires verified ownership, an active auth client, and proven local routing, while unset requires the domain to exist, and a second set preserves the one-canonical invariant by atomically replacing the existing canonical row. These preconditions are checked before any state mutation."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Spans the full platform sign-in surface: login initiates a PKCE/state/nonce redirect handoff, the callback validates state/code/nonce and resolves identity into a server-side session, session reads return authenticated or unauthenticated context, and logout idempotently destroys session and clears host-only plus domain-scoped cookies. It also covers IdP and policy administration lifecycles (list/create/update/rotate-secret/enable/disable/delete identity providers, OIDC discovery import, and read/validate/write of MFA, lockout, session, and claim-mapping policy). Each administrative mutation resolves the tenant credential, audits, then writes to the identity provider and may be read back."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Starting a workflow requires a workflow key, tenant, and workflow id; signal names drive only explicit, named transitions; a denied approval deterministically fails the workflow; and unknown workflow reads or invalid route ids surface as typed route/use-case errors. Provider adapters validate and normalise upstream status before it reaches the canonical state machine, so malformed provider responses cannot corrupt workflow state."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State comprises a static default theme plus tenant-scoped theme override keys consumed by the runtime theme response, alongside registry-managed branding definitions (application name typed as a string and a theme selection constrained to system/light/dark). Bootstrap theme state and editable branding-registry state are kept distinct so the pre-auth response stays simple while managed edits carry full definition semantics."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State comprises catalog entries with lineage, dataset classifications constrained to none, PII, or sensitive, and data-subject-request records constrained to open or fulfilled, with a fulfilment-evidence payload attached on completion. The classification and request constraints are defined by a governance migration and the evidence payload was added by a later forward migration to preserve checksum stability of the original. Lineage and catalog metadata describe datasets without copying their sensitive contents."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State comprises preferences keyed by organisation, user, channel, and category with an enabled flag; a notification log with status sent|suppressed|failed; channel transports of email|webhook|local; resolved recipients; and per-channel readiness availability. This capability holds tenant data, so its records participate in tenant backup, export, retention, and legal-hold semantics. Recipient resolution and preference state are tenant-scoped and audit metadata deliberately excludes secret-bearing payloads."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State comprises the secret ref, organisationId, name, provider in postgres|openbao, version, a revoked flag, the backend path, an encrypted_value for the built-in Postgres store or null when the value lives in OpenBao, and created, updated, and deleted metadata; list and getMetadata responses carry no value. The built-in store encrypts the value at rest while OpenBao holds the value entirely outside Postgres. Metadata is tenant-scoped under row-level security so refs do not leak across organisations."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State comprises workerId, workerKind, a heartbeat timestamp, liveness in alive|stale|stopped, the status of the claimed event, a retry count, and the dead-letter transition; the runner does not own tenant records and reads pending and dead-letter queues from the event-bus state model. Idempotency is anchored on the event's processed status so a re-delivered or reclaimed event is not processed twice. Liveness is derived from heartbeat age rather than stored as a separate authoritative flag."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State comprises workflowId, workflowKey, tenantId, payload, a status of running|waiting|completed|failed|cancelled, a free-form detail field, and provider readiness, governed by a canAccess(workflowId, tenantId) predicate that binds every workflow to its owning tenant. Provider adapters map Temporal or HTTP statuses onto these canonical status values so the state machine is provider-independent. Cross-tenant access is denied by orchestrator semantics rather than by convention."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State includes account/customer external account identifier, subscription identifier with status (active, paused, cancelled), associated plan and price, invoice status with open amount and currency, payment charge outcome keyed by an idempotency key, and refund success state. Amount, currency, and status fields are kept explicit and the financial ledger is treated as append-only so prior outcomes are not overwritten."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State includes API keys in active or revoked state with prefix, scopes, and created/revoked metadata and no plaintext secret, developer portal summaries, the OpenAPI route contract and GraphQL contract, and rate-limit policy plus per-window count and exceeded state. Only a key prefix and hash are retained, never the raw secret."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State includes each service's key, name, and category; its environment model; visibility (tenant_scoped_safe, global_only, or not_exposed); the integration decision (build, compose, adapter, defer, or reject); the entitlement key; proof references; console-access flags; readiness status; and provider details. Database changes use ordered SQL migrations that must preserve this proven state model, and rollback is forward-fix or guarded restore after migration lineage is verified so tenant data is never silently dropped or remapped. As a tenant-data participant it is subject to tenant backup/export/retention/legal-hold semantics."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State includes host classifications (apex, slug, reserved, unknown, malformed, custom domain), the resolved tenant context (organisation identifier, slug, host source), the row-level-security tenant setting in the database, the object-storage tenant prefix, and a null tenant context for untrusted hosts. Host source distinguishes slug-resolved from active verified custom-domain resolution."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State includes providerKey, capability, environment, instanceLabel, classification, lifecycleState (proposed, configured, ready, degraded, disabled), endpoint, config, credentialRef, requiresCredential, and audit metadata. Database changes use ordered SQL migrations that must preserve this proven state model, and rollback is forward-fix or guarded restore after migration lineage is verified. Credentials are referenced rather than embedded, keeping secret material out of the configuration record."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State includes static-analysis rule severities, the SBOM baseline document and lock hash, SBOM policy audit output, code-scanning config/database/result state, security-route registration, and the global security-console clickthrough readiness. The state is configuration and evidence rather than owned tenant records."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State includes tenant admin credential lifecycle metadata, identity-provider secret presence with provider-masked values, secret stores for mail/webhook/API-key surfaces, and a token-crypto state distinguishing encrypted values from an explicit unencrypted test marker, all classified for readiness without ever materialising raw secret output. The persisted representation deliberately holds only protected or metadata forms of each secret."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State includes the extracted route method/path set, the OpenAPI path/method entries, the missing-route set, the extra-documented-route set, unresolved references, the schemaless-operation list, and a strict versus report-only exit decision. There is no owned database; state is the computed comparison between the live routes and the documented contract."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State includes the flattened locale key map, the duplicate list, the used-key set, interpolation parameter usage, raw-literal findings, governed/exclude/exception configuration, the strictFailOnRawLiteral flag, and the strict/report-only exit state. Database changes use ordered migrations that must preserve this proven model. The state is the validation corpus over translation keys rather than owned tenant data."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State includes the organisation id, slug/FQDN, a derived realm name of the form tenant-{organisationId}, a host source (slug, custom_domain, or fixture), and the per-FQDN domain-registry states for custom domains. A custom domain only contributes tenant context once it is verified and active."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State includes the organisation identifier, generated-at timestamp, metrics signals, open-incident count, legal-hold count, retention-policy count, storage readiness fields, and a ready boolean. Counts and readiness fields are computed from injected foundation sources at generation time."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State includes the subscription (identifier, URL, subscribed event types, enabled flag, secret hash) and per-delivery state of pending, delivered, failed, or dead with attempt count, next-attempt time, and last-status metrics, plus a redrive-pending reset. Readiness state is classified as no-subscriptions, configured, or has-dead-deliveries, and only the secret hash is stored rather than the plaintext secret."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State includes the support ticket (identifier, subject, body, status, organisation, actor, timestamps), customer-health signals derived from tickets and metered usage, the announcement (identifier, subject, message, creator, created-at), and support-mode approval/session state in the adjacent approval proof. Health is a computed read-model over tickets and usage rather than a stored score."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is a canonical boolean plus a canonical timestamp and the redirect policy, constrained so at most one enabled canonical domain exists per tenant. Canonical is a marker only: it does not upgrade routing status or TLS status, which remain governed by their own lifecycle."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is a delegated-role record carrying id, organisation id, granter and grantee user ids, scope, granted timestamp and grantor, optional expiry, and revoked timestamp and revoker. Activeness is derived from the revoked and expiry fields."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is a host classification kind (apex, tenant_slug, reserved_subdomain, invalid_subdomain, possible_custom_domain, or malformed) plus, when resolved, a tenant context containing organisation id, slug, realm name, and host source. Untrusted classifications carry no tenant context."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is a meter catalog (meter key, entitlement key, display name, unit) plus meter-event rows containing organisation, meter, quantity, idempotency key, subject/source/metadata, and occurred-at time. The idempotency key participates in event identity so a replayed event does not double-count, and negative adjustments are stored as explicit events rather than mutating prior rows."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is a quota record (quota key, entitlement key, meter key, limit, window, deny action, updated-at/updated-by) plus a computed evaluation state of within, exceeded, no-entitlement, or no-quota, together with current usage, an allowed flag, and a projected usage value for delta checks. Usage is derived from the metering aggregate rather than stored independently."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is a tenant-realm group identified by id, name, and path, with reserved names protected; groups live in the identity provider's realm and are not persisted in the relational store. The group set is scoped to the tenant realm."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is a tenant-scoped membership carrying user id, organisation id, tenant role, optional username, status (invited, active, or disabled), creation/update/last-login timestamps, and inviter, alongside separate pending-invitation rows. Membership is always scoped to one organisation."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is a three-level hierarchy: Product (identifier, name, description, active flag, created timestamp), Plan (identifier, owning product, name, currency, billing period, active flag, created timestamp), and Price (identifier, owning plan, version, price type, unit amount, currency, billing period, active flag, created timestamp). Items carry explicit active/inactive state rather than being hard-deleted, and price versioning preserves historical amounts. State changes flow through ordered migrations that must preserve this proven model."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is active versus revoked, with creation and last-used timestamps, an optional expiry, a revoked timestamp, a key prefix, scopes, and hash/salt storage fields. The plaintext secret is explicitly not part of persisted state."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is an audit-event projection carrying id, action, actor id, resource, resource id, timestamp, and redacted metadata, where logical resources map to member, config, feature, and auth-settings contexts. The capability projects existing durable rows rather than owning new mutable state."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is an organisation id plus entitlement key with a state of granted or revoked alongside source, metadata, update timestamp, and updater, while the tenant self-read view projects every catalog key into granted, revoked, or not-granted. Feature flags are explicitly distinct from entitlements."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is an organisation row carrying parent id, slug, display name, active flag, and timestamps, exposed to the API as a flat tenant-scoped list while the parent id is kept internal. Children are always anchored to a resolved parent tenant."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is each guarded route's resource, scope, and required permission, plus optional resource-policy records and a decision result that is one of granted, policy-denied, insufficient-auth-level, server-unavailable, or resource-not-registered, with a static permission fallback. The decision is derived per request rather than stored."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is held in a single canonical relational database with two tenant-isolation layers: a schema-per-tenant model where per-tenant configuration lives in tenant-scoped schemas selected by a transaction-local search path, and public-schema tenant-scoped tables carrying a tenant/organisation identifier column protected by row-level security. The migration ledger table tracks each applied file name (unique), its checksum, and apply timestamp; checksum is the first 16 hex characters of the SHA-256 of the committed file bytes, computed over the file with secret placeholders intact so it is identical across every environment.
