Tenant-scoped tables ENABLE and FORCE row-level security; provider substrates such as cache, search, and analytics are adapters behind ports and never own canonical schema."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is split between a pure, serialisable registry of configuration definitions (each carrying storage key, value type such as string/enum/boolean/json, allowed values, tenant-overridability, lifecycle, and per-definition read/write permissions) and the persisted tenant override values. The effective value carries a source marker distinguishing platform default from tenant override, and feature-flag compatibility transforms are applied during resolution."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is tenant-and-user-scoped: a profile (display name, locale, timezone), a preference set (channel, category, enabled flag), and a durable dispatch log status of sent, suppressed, or failed. There are no secret-bearing columns in the self-service state."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is the domain's auth-client status (inactive or active) together with an activation timestamp, the canonical flag, routing status, and a disabled guard. If the auth-client port throws during activation the active marker is never written, so registry state cannot drift ahead of the external configuration."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is the environment registry behind a port (environment-registry-repository): the set of registered environments and the manifest-derived configuration each one bootstraps, recovered from the cited migration and usecase source as lineage. The state is configuration/evidence-shaped and owns no tenant data, so restore cannot create tenant records. Bootstrap derives generated environment configuration deterministically from manifests rather than inventing defaults."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is the role vocabulary split into a global role (system-admin) and tenant roles (tenant-admin, manager, member, viewer), with role-to-permission bundles resolved through a fixed permission map and membership status tracked separately. The resolved permission set, not the role name, is what downstream authorization consumes."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is the scheduled_jobs table holding organisationId, jobKey, eventType, intervalSeconds, an enabled flag, nextRunAt, and lastRunAt, together with an event idempotency window that prevents duplicate enqueue within the same due window. Enqueued jobs materialise as platform_events on the shared event substrate, so downstream state, ordering, retry, and dead-letter follow the event-bus state model. Row-level security scopes scheduled jobs to the owning organisation."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State is the support approval workflow id and status plus the support session id, a support-mode flag, the effective and target organisation/tenant ids, the access reason, roles, a time-to-live of one hour, and explicitly no tenant-scoped permissions. The session carries break-glass context rather than ordinary tenant membership."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State-changing access preserves tenant context through route, use-case, and provider spans, and typed error logs carry the tenant/organisation identifier when the operation is tenant-scoped. The migration ledger is itself an audit trail: each applied file is recorded with its checksum and timestamp, and historical files retain their decision-reference comment blocks so that later forward corrections remain traceable to the file they supersede. Recovery and restore must preserve tenant boundary, audit, and data-subject evidence."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State-changing and security-relevant actions emit audit records before the effect is acknowledged, so the audit trail cannot diverge from what actually happened. Audit entries preserve tenant boundary, request/trace correlation, and DSR/GDPR evidence requirements, and a missing tenant-isolation or audit signal is itself an alertable condition."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State-changing catalog and integration actions follow audit-before-mutation behaviour recovered from the source lineage and tests, recording the actor and change so the tenant boundary and DSR/GDPR evidence are preserved. Audit and readiness signals stay visible in degraded mode. Recovery preserves tenant boundary and audit evidence rather than silently overwriting it."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State-changing environment-registry operations follow audit-before-mutation behaviour recovered from the cited source, recording who registered or bootstrapped an environment. Audit and readiness signals remain visible in degraded mode. This preserves an honest, inspectable history of environment registration and bootstrap."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"State-changing provider-config operations follow audit-before-mutation behaviour with audit metadata on the record, capturing who changed a provider's configuration or lifecycle state. Audit and readiness signals remain visible in degraded mode. This preserves an honest, inspectable history of provider configuration changes."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Static-analysis error findings, a missing or stale SBOM, policy violations, missing code-scanning in authoritative mode, an invalid code-scanning configuration, or an absent route all fail non-zero. Authoritative mode fails closed so a missing gate cannot be treated as a pass."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Sub-organisation lifecycle is list active child organisations, create with a slug and display name, update the display name, and deactivate by clearing the active flag. Deactivation is a soft state change rather than a hard delete."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Subscription, invoice, payment, and dunning operations are scoped to the owning tenant for reads while provider-affecting actions are operator-controlled; cross-tenant access to billing records is prevented. Authorization is enforced server-side before any provider call."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Substrate and unit proofs cover login routes, the auth usecase, session fixtures, cookie security, token crypto, role/permission resolution, and audit-first ordering, while runtime proofs validate live identity-provider settings round-trips, IdP CRUD with secret rotation and redaction, OIDC discovery/JWKS/callback/test-connection, MFA and session policy write/read-back/restore, the claim-mapping semantic journey, and custom-domain callback derivation against local substrate. Proof is hermetic/runtime lineage; fresh proof remains pending."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Subsystem failures propagate as typed or ordinary errors and halt later destructive steps; for example a realm-deletion failure leaves the recorded calls at export, delete-storage, delete-realm with no further deletion. Failures fail closed so partial destruction does not silently complete."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Support and announcement operations are tenant/operator-scoped through platform support permissions and actor-role metadata, and support-approval access is gated before a support session is created. Tenant context cannot read another tenant's tickets, health, or announcements."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Support session creation emits a support-session-created audit-before-change event, the approval request emits an audit with the requested state and workflow id, and audit failure results in no support session. Audit precedes session creation, and this capability is the producer whose privileged-access audit evidence the audit-of-privileged-access capability depends on."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Support-access lifecycle is request-approval moving an approval workflow to waiting, then approval completing it and creating an audited time-boxed support session scoped to exactly one target tenant; a direct enter-support-mode path creates the same scoped session after validation. The session is deliberately short-lived (one hour)."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Suspend and delete emit audit before subsystem coordination, and both unit and runtime proof assert that the audit is invoked first. Lifecycle transitions are audited so provisioning, suspension, deletion, and export are attributable."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Tenant developer reads use a tenant developer-read permission, operator policy read/write use platform rate-limit permissions, and policy evaluation additionally requires the configured entitlement. Operator routes validate the tenant identifier and policy mutation is operator-only."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Tenant identity covers provisioning of a tenant record and resolution of request hosts to that tenant: apex, reserved, invalid, and malformed hosts resolve to no tenant, seeded slug FQDNs resolve with a slug host source, and active verified custom domains resolve through the domain registry with a custom-domain host source. Provisioning is operator-driven and host resolution is a deterministic per-request derivation."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Tenant lifecycle state is represented by coordinated subsystem outcomes and export metadata: suspend returns coordinated [data, storage, realm, DSR]; delete returns coordinated [export, storage, realm, DSR, data] plus an export digest and key reference. The export is produced before deletion so a portable archive exists prior to destructive steps."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Tenant operations require tenant API-key read/write permissions and operator read requires the platform API-key read permission, and creation additionally requires an API-access entitlement that is deny-by-default. Tenant isolation prevents one tenant from listing another tenant's keys."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Tenant provisioning is audited at the provisioning surface, while host-identity resolution is read-only and carries no mutation audit, with failed resolution logged rather than audited. Audit precedes the provisioning change."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Tenant provisioning is operator-controlled and gated by platform tenant read/create permissions, while host-identity resolution is read-only request context that grants no data access without the route's own permission checks. Tenant isolation is preserved because resolution never produces a partial or fallback tenant."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Tenant quota reads are tenant-scoped and operator set/update operations require operator authorization for a specified tenant; evaluation additionally requires the configured entitlement. Cross-tenant quota access is prevented and policy mutation is operator-only."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Tenant read requires the tenant entitlements read permission and operator read/write require the platform entitlements read/write permissions, and policy-chain evaluation denies on missing permission before evaluating entitlement. Cross-tenant grants do not leak across the tenant boundary."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Tenant webhook operations require a tenant webhooks permission and are scoped to the requesting organisation, with redrive and test actions requiring the same tenant context and actor metadata. Cross-tenant delivery rows are hidden by organisation identifier so one tenant cannot see another's deliveries."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"The a11y gate owns no tenant data and exposes no tenant-mutating routes, so standard platform security controls apply; the gate is an operator/CI concern rather than an end-user permission. Accessibility expectations apply to UI surfaces for all users and are not tenant-gated. Configuring exceptions is a governance authority, not an end-user role."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"The abacpolicydecisionpoint capability is explicitly API-only; no human-rendered surface, component, action, journey, consent prompt, or renderer input is authorised. Any UI requires a deliberate exposure amendment."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string
"The accessibilitya11ygate capability is explicitly internal; no product or operator UI is authorised. Any UI requires a deliberate exposure amendment."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"The apidocsdeveloperportalsdksratelimits capability has one framework-neutral UI semantic model with explicit surfaces, view models, components, journeys, permissions, accessibility, localisation, and target-specific renderer contracts. This semantic closure disclaims product parity, human acceptance, accessibility compliance, and launch-language readiness."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"The apikeyspersonalaccesstokens capability has one framework-neutral UI semantic model with explicit surfaces, view models, components, journeys, permissions, accessibility, localisation, and target-specific renderer contracts. This semantic closure disclaims product parity, human acceptance, accessibility compliance, and launch-language readiness."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"The assertion path throws a typed forbidden error when not entitled, the evaluation path returns a denied decision by permission or entitlement, and invalid tenant or key cases return 400; provider failure returns a typed degraded result fail-closed. Access defaults to denied when state is missing."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"The audit trail is the decision record lineage: every build-versus-compose determination is captured as a reviewable, versioned governance artefact rather than a runtime mutation log. Changes must update the semantic artefacts and re-run the named proof so the rationale stays auditable. This preserves honest lineage of why a capability was built or composed."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string
"The auditofprivilegedaccess capability is explicitly not exposed; no product or operator UI is authorised. Any UI requires a deliberate exposure amendment."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"The authenticationplatform capability has one framework-neutral UI semantic model with explicit surfaces, view models, components, journeys, permissions, accessibility, localisation, and target-specific renderer contracts. This semantic closure disclaims product parity, human acceptance, accessibility compliance, and launch-language readiness."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string
"The backgroundworkersjobrunner capability is explicitly internal; no product or operator UI is authorised. Any UI requires a deliberate exposure amendment."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string
"The backupandrestore capability is explicitly not exposed; no product or operator UI is authorised. Any UI requires a deliberate exposure amendment."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string
"The brandingandtheming capability is explicitly not exposed; no product or operator UI is authorised. Any UI requires a deliberate exposure amendment."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"The browsertelemetrygrafanafarorumandbrowsertobfftracing capability is explicitly internal; no product or operator UI is authorised. Any UI requires a deliberate exposure amendment."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"The buildversuscomposedecisionframework capability is explicitly internal; no product or operator UI is authorised. Any UI requires a deliberate exposure amendment."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"The capability assigns roles and deterministically resolves them into permissions: tenant membership roles (tenant-admin, manager, member, viewer) are assigned through the member role-update path, system-admin is a global role that is rejected as a membership role, and any role change re-resolves the actor's permission bundle. Roles are convenience bundles while permissions are the enforcement primitive."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"The capability exposes a governance catalog with lineage plus data-subject-request routes, and interacts with other capabilities (cross-capability interactions are recorded) because lineage and classification draw on tenant foundation signals. "The runtimesecretsmanagement capability is explicitly internal; no product or operator UI is authorised. Any UI requires a deliberate exposure amendment."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"The serverlessfunctionruntime capability is explicitly internal; no product or operator UI is authorised. Any UI requires a deliberate exposure amendment."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

State changes are governed by deliberate semantic decisions rather than runtime mutations."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"The state is the ladder definition and the aggregated confidence over its stages: the registry of e2e journeys, their required stages, and the per-stage pass/fail roll-up, held as configuration and evidence rather than owned tenant rows. It has no owned database schema, so backup scope is configuration/evidence only and restore cannot create tenant data. Each stage's posture is tracked independently so a higher stage cannot inherit a lower stage's proof."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"The state is the per-service classification (environment-specific vs shared) and the routing/isolation rules derived from it, held as configuration rather than owned tenant rows. Classification changes propagate to how services are resolved per environment."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"The state is the recorded decision corpus rather than tenant rows: per-capability the chosen disposition (build/compose/adapter/defer/reject) with its rationale, criteria scores, and supersession history. It has no owned database schema; changes are limited to contract/config references and the governing document. It owns no tenant data, so backup is configuration/evidence only and restore cannot create tenant data."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"The state is the set of accessibility expectations and the latest gate results rather than owned tenant rows: the required landmarks, roles, ARIA attributes, and axe rule outcomes per audited surface, held as configuration and evidence. "Typed outcomes include invalid-name, conflict, not-found, protected, and ok, mapped fail-closed to 400/409/404/422/201/204, and a missing tenant credential returns a no-credential/503 result; provider failure keeps mutation boundaries closed. "Typed outcomes include ok, static-permission-denied, delegation-already-active, and not-found, and denied paths log warnings while emitting no audit or mutation; provider failure returns a typed degraded result fail-closed. "Unit proofs cover the delegation state machine and the storage adapter and a runtime proof covers the local composition, demonstrated in source lineage via hermetic state-machine and audit-order validation. "Unit proofs cover the profile and notification usecases, and runtime proofs validate live profile self-service, notification preferences, and dispatch against the data substrate with row-level tenant isolation, demonstrated in source lineage via hermetic/runtime validation. Duplicate idempotency keys resolve to the original event without double-counting, and provider unavailability returns a typed degraded failure rather than a fabricated success."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

Validation never opens an unregistered resource by default."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Untrusted hosts resolve to a null tenant context, absent or unverified custom domains are rejected, foreign tenant data is hidden or rejected, and provider failures degrade readiness rather than falling back to an unsafe tenant. The system fails closed to no-tenant rather than guessing a tenant."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Untrusted or unresolved hosts return a null tenant context fail-closed, and global routes reject apex subdomains with an explicit detail rather than silently serving global content; provider failure returns a typed degraded result. No host is ever resolved to a fallback tenant."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Uploads validate content type and size against quota and place the object under the correct tenant prefix; the scan lifecycle validates an object as clean before it is treated as usable, quarantining or rejecting otherwise. Tenant context is required so registry access and prefixes are correctly scoped. Missing or invalid configuration fails closed rather than defaulting to an open bucket."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Usecase results include a not-entitled and an ok variant, invalid route identifiers return 400, and revoked or malformed secrets authenticate as no actor; provider failure returns a typed degraded result fail-closed. Authentication failures never leak whether a key existed."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

In strict mode (strictFailOnRawLiteral) it fails closed and returns a non-zero exit; in report-only mode it surfaces findings without blocking. The used-key set is reconciled against the locale key map so drift is caught at gate time."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Validation checks static-analysis error findings, SBOM file integrity and lock hash, license/security policy, code-scanning binary/config/database behaviour with an authoritative fail-closed mode, and route registration. Where configured, a locally absent code-scanning tool may honestly skip rather than silently pass."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Validation checks that each decision is complete, justified against the stated criteria, and consistent with the authority order and naming rules, and that a decision does not contradict downstream semantic contracts. Decisions that would upgrade proof posture or treat composed providers as more proven than evidence allows are rejected."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Validation enforces required fields per provider, that credentialRef is present when requiresCredential is set, and that lifecycleState transitions are legal (for example, a provider cannot be ready without valid configuration). Inputs are validated before mutation and invalid configuration fails closed. Health is probed before a provider is allowed to reach the ready state."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Validation enforces that each catalog entry has a coherent decision, visibility, entitlement, and readiness state, that tenant-scoped exposure is safe, and that provider details resolve. Inputs are checked before mutation and missing or invalid configuration fails closed. It guards against exposing a service more broadly than its visibility classification permits."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Validation enforces that each stage's required journeys ran and passed and that confidence is aggregated honestly, never letting a hermetic pass stand in for an integration, staging, or production-shaped pass. Inputs are the e2e results per stage, which must be present and current. Missing, stale, or unknown stage results are treated as not-pass."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Validation enforces that the foundation's invariants hold across the corpus: proof level is not report status, readiness claims must not exceed observed evidence, hermetic proof must not be upgraded to live external proof, and production-shaped must not be treated as production-live. It validates the asset graph for semantic drift and configuration loss, and treats stale or unknown signals as not-pass. Inputs that would violate the authority order or naming rules are rejected at the governance boundary."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Validation enforces the cross-dimension safety rules: provider mode and environment stay independent, hermetic-mock must not satisfy live-external-provider, and production-shaped must not satisfy production-live. Inputs are the per-provider posture declarations, which must be consistent and complete. Any classification that would upgrade posture by implication is rejected."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

Bootstrap refuses to fabricate values that the manifest does not declare."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Validation ensures every relevant service has an explicit, consistent classification and that shared-versus-specific assignments do not violate environment isolation. Drift or configuration loss is the failure to guard against. Misclassification that would cross an environment boundary is rejected."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Validation ensures the aggregation faithfully reflects each provider's readiness and never reports the spine as ready when any required composed provider is degraded or unknown. Inputs are the per-provider readiness states, which must resolve before the roll-up is trusted. A stale or unknown provider state must not be counted as pass."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Validation failures return safe validation-error responses, no-tenant writes return a 400 no-tenant outcome, and secret-bearing notification payloads raise an explicit not-notifiable error; provider failure returns a typed degraded result fail-closed. No partial profile state is persisted on failure."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string

"Validation proves a clean repository exits strict with success, missing and extra routes are detected, unresolved references are detected, schemaless bodies are detected, bodyless status responses are exempted, and the live document has no schemaless bodies or dangling references. Strict mode is the enforced configuration."^^http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#string
